articleTitle: New methods for determining the vacancy and void content of single crystal silicon
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given. Our present understanding of the point defect concentration and atomic transport in pure silicon will be reviewed, with the emphasis on the loss of equilibrium as the temperature is lowered. Diffusion and trapping of "fast" impurities in silicon will be reviewed. Interstitial in- and out-diffusion at low temperature of impurities that may be trapped at vacancies and internal surfaces provides new opportunities for characterizing lattice defects.

articleTitle: AC and DC voltage standards based on silicon micromechanics
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Micromechanical AC and DC standards, suitable for compact, low-cost precision electronics applications are described. The standards are based on controlling the charge of a parallel-moving-plate capacitor. We expect that the voltage standards based on mechanical and geometrical properties of single crystalline silicon can have a high stability. We show the basic principle of the AC and DC standards and preliminary experiments with the AC voltage standard.

articleTitle: Thermal transfer measurements at microwatt power levels
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and preliminary results for a thermal transfer standard operating at a power level of 20 /spl mu/W, or less, and at temperatures below 10 K. The new converter employs a superconducting-resistive-transition edge thermometer.

articleTitle: A broadband technique for one-port VNA calibration and characterization of low-loss two-ports
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A broadband versatile technique for precision one-port calibration of VNA is presented. It is an extension of a previous sliding short method, but accommodating a broader class of calibration devices, such as delayed short and open circuits. It features a high measurement redundancy that allows the delays and losses of these devices to be determined during the calibration. The new method is suitable for measurement of low-loss two-ports.

articleTitle: Free-space transmission method for wide-band microwave wheat permittivity measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A free-space transmission technique was used to determine the dielectric properties of wheat at frequencies from 4 to 12 GHz. Undesirable effects such as multiple reflections and diffraction at the edges of the sample were minimized by selecting optimum conditions and use of a microwave focused beam.

articleTitle: Calibration method for four-terminal-pair capacitance standards: Progress report
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper titled "A New Universal Calibration Method for Four-Terminal-Pair Admittance Standards" (1991) described briefly a calibration method for commercially available four-terminal-pair capacitance standards (4TP C STDs). Since we established an accurate calibration method for the 4TP C STDs using a network analyzer and a 1 kHz capacitance bridge, this paper describes the method for a 1000 pF air dielectric 4TP C STD at 10 MHz.

articleTitle: A bridge for the comparison of resistance with capacitance at frequencies from 0.2 to 2 kHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A bridge for the comparison of resistance with capacitance in the frequency range 0.2 to 2 kHz has been designed. It is a six-arm generalization of the quad bridge, and makes extensive use of precision amplifiers in both source and detector circuits. It will provide a link between the calculable capacitor and the ac QHR.

articleTitle: A new scheme for generating and measuring active, reactive and apparent power at power frequencies with uncertainties of 5 ppm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new method for generating and measuring active, reactive and apparent power at power frequencies has been devised. It makes use of digital signal synthesis and DFT evaluation based on a single master clock. This results in a significant reduction of synchronizing errors and thus in an uncertainty of 5 ppm.

articleTitle: Combined optical-infrared single ion frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A combined infrared-optical frequency standard scheme has been demonstrated using a single ion of ytterbium. The optical /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ reference transition at 411 nm and the infrared /sup 2/F/sub 7/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ 3.43 μm transition were driven sequentially. A measurement of the 3.43 μm transition frequency has been made.

articleTitle: Realization of the farad at BNM-LCIE
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The BNM-LCIE Thompson Lampard Calculable Capacitance (TLCC) has been taken apart for improvements between 1994 and 1997. Influencing parameters were determined and/or corrected: parallelism of the electrodes, end effects, dimensions of a compensating spike and effect of its lateral displacement. With these improvements and by using a new interferometer, the realization of the farad is achieved with an uncertainty (not taking into account the frequency dependance of the TLCC) equal to 3 10/sup -8/ (1/spl sigma/).

articleTitle: A sensor for electric and magnetic-field measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper presents a method for measuring the electric and magnetic field with one sensor. The solution suggested is a simple one, and makes possible the extension, under 100 kHz, of the frequency range of the sensors used for electric and magnetic field measurements in the same place in space.

articleTitle: Effect of substrate thickness and permittivity on the characteristics of rectangular microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The most important factors in design of microstrip circuit and antenna are choice of the best substrate thickness and the dielectric constant to have low losses. Most of the work on microstrip antenna in the past, employed electrically thin and low permittivity substrates. In this case an attempt has been made by selecting various dielectric constants and thicknesses to study various parameters. For this, a rectangular microstrip antenna (RMSA) is designed in X-band at 9.2 GHz and fabricated on different substrates ranging dielectric constant between 2.20 to 10.20 and thickness ranging 0.635 mm to 1.574 mm. The return loss of of the order of -43 dB is also observed at the designed frequency. The bandwidth in between 4% to 20% was observed.

articleTitle: Automatization of the multifunctions laboratory
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The work done consisted in the implementation of a multifunction laboratory with the objective of calibrating universal calibrators and 8 1/2 digits multimeters, based on an automatic system through IEEE-488 interface, developed using Labview software.

articleTitle: A system to measure current transducer performance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A special purpose ac current transducer measurement system capable of intercomparing transducers with ac output voltage ratios from 1:1 to 50:1 has been developed to extend the range and accuracy of current transformer, current shunt, and mutual inductor calibrations at power frequencies of 50 Hz and 60 Hz. The system consists of a two-stage binary inductive voltage divider, an amplifier-aided two-stage current transformer, a precision shunt, a wideband buffer, and a commercial, sampling digital multimeter (DMM). When comparing current transducers with ac output voltage ratios of 1:1 to 50:1, the system attains an overall relative standard uncertainty of the ratio of 10/sup -5/ to 10/sup -4/, respectively. The basic system can be used to calibrate transducers with input currents of 0.1 A to 200 A (RMS) and can be extended to measure devices handling input currents up to 15 kA.

articleTitle: Development of a self-calibration precision electrical measuring meter
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. This presentation describes a mathematical analog model, method of calibration, circuit characteristics and error analysis of electrical energy, power, voltage and current meter at power frequency based on a self-calibration principle. Results of comparison of the prototype meters and their test results are also presented.

articleTitle: AC-DC voltage transfer difference due to Seebeck effect in thermal converters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The AC-DC transfer difference of a single-junction thermal converter can be evaluated with an uncertainty of the order of 0.1 ppm using a fast-reversed DC source. At this level of uncertainty the dependence of the AC-DC voltage transfer difference on the value of the range resistor has been measured. It is shown that the Seebeck effect in the heater/heater support lead junction is responsible for this behavior.

articleTitle: Temperature compensated cryogenic whispering gallery mode resonator for microwave frequency standard applications
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have investigated a miniature composite dielectric resonator employing a sapphire puck and a single crystalline platelet of rutile, excited in a whispering gallery mode. We have achieved values of the Allan variance as low as 4/spl times/10/sup -12/ for an integration time of 1000 seconds with the prototype system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of low-frequency voltage dividers, using the step response
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A method to characterize the behavior of low frequency voltage dividers, based on the step response, is presented. Amplitude errors and phase displacements can be evaluated, in an absolute way, without any auxiliary standard divider.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical waveguide W-band spectrometer for precision dielectric measurement of absorbing materials
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A quasi-optical waveguide bridge spectrometer is designed and constructed for the precision measurement of dielectric permittivity and loss tangent of medium and highly absorbing materials over an extended W-band frequency range. An electronically sweeping backward wave oscillator (BWO) is used as a source of tunable coherent radiation in the frequency range 70-118 GHz. The high output power of BWO (typically 50-100 mW at each frequency) and high sensitivity receiver system employing a liquid helium cooled InSb detector enable the accurate transmission measurement of highly absorbing materials. Data for very absorbing materials such as the low resistivity silicon and germanium are presented and compared.

articleTitle: AC high voltage standard of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Herein the structure of AC high voltage standard and methods included in its basis are described. The important role of high harmonized components of voltage and their influence and the way of standard's error expression are considered herein.

articleTitle: G measurement with the dynamic free pendulum method: first results
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper presents some preliminary results about the measurement of G with the dynamic pendulum method. Although the uncertainty is still high (20%), the measurements are well centered on the known value of G. Present problems of the experiment are discussed and solutions to reach the projected accuracy of the method are proposed.

articleTitle: A method for calibration of partial discharge calibrators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A method for calibration of partial discharge calibrators has been developed based on passive integration of the induced charge. The voltage over a known capacitor is measured by a calibrated digital sampling voltmeter and the charge is calculated as the voltage multiplied by the capacitance. The best achieved uncertainty is /spl plusmn/2% for a coverage factor k=2.

articleTitle: Capacitance intercomparison between NML (South Africa) and NPL (India) and NML (South Africa) and NMi (Netherlands)
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The National Metrology Laboratory (NML) of South Africa carried out two independent capacitance intercomparisons with the Nederlands Meetinstituut (NMi) of the Netherlands and the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) of India during the latter part of 1997. The paper gives the results of the intercomparison and the capacitance measurement systems prevalent in the laboratories involved.

articleTitle: Accuracy characterization of arbitrary waveform generators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The possibility to employ an arbitrary waveform generator as a reference source for complex waveforms depends on its performance and determined accuracy. This paper suggests an approach to characterization based on a simple mathematical model of a digital signal generator and on tests using only sinewave generation.

articleTitle: Comparison of high voltage thermal converter scaling to a binary inductive voltage divider
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: High-voltage thermal converters (HVTCs) are used as standards of AC-DC difference and for the measurement and calibration of AC voltage up to 1000 V and 100 kHz. Their multiplying resistors can be compensated to yield small AC-DC differences by using adjustable internal shields; however, the AC-DC differences of HVTCs may vary as functions of warm-up time, applied frequency, and applied voltage. Voltage coefficients between 100 V and 1000 V can be quite significant compared to calibration uncertainties, and can be major sources of error in the buildup process used to characterize the HVTCs. Formal and informal international intercomparisons of HVTCs have revealed variations among the participating laboratories. The present work was undertaken to compare the scaling accuracy of HVTCs to the completely independent principle of a binary inductive voltage divider.

articleTitle: Coaxial calculable AC resistor
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The principle of a new type of AC resistance standard with calculable frequency characteristics is proposed. The resistive element is a short stick of ceramics covered of a metallic thin film (Ni-Cr). The standard is defined in 5 terminals or in 4 terminal pairs configuration. The calculation of characteristics has been made both with analytic and numerical methods. These calculations permitted to define the geometry of the standard in order to get a time constant lower than 10 ps for a 10 k/spl Omega/ resistance (up to a few megahertz).

articleTitle: Optical frequency measurement of the acetylene transitions at 1.5 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on an optical frequency measurement of the acetylene transitions at 1.5 /spl mu/m. Using an optical frequency comb generator and second harmonic generation, we can directly connect an acetylene-stabilized diode laser to a 778 nm diode laser stabilized on a reference Rb two-photon transition.

articleTitle: Comparison of capacitance with AC quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A quadrature bridge to compare 10 nF capacitances to the i=2 plateau of the quantized Hall resistance is being developed to realize the farad directly at a frequency of 1.233 kHz. Portable precision ceramic capacitance transfer standards of remarkable performance have been developed for this purpose.

articleTitle: Reproduction of the ohm based on the quantum Hall effect at CENAM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A quantum Hall resistance standard has been implemented at CENAM to reproduce the electrical resistance unit. As a first step of this project we have used the digital voltmeter method for the measurement of the quantized Hall resistance and standard resistors.

articleTitle: Sampling power meter for low frequencies (45-55 Hz)
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have developed a new wattmeter based on digital sampling techniques. A unique feature of the system is the incorporation of the power source needed to feed the standard and device under test which greatly helps avoiding synchronisation problems. A bilateral comparison with SP in Sweden using a Pupin type travelling standard show good agreement between the results.

articleTitle: Design and verification of a 24 kA calibration head for a DCCT test facility [for LHC]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is CERN's next particle accelerator project, scheduled to be commissioned in 2005. The project requires accurate current measurements above 10 kA. Calibration heads have been developed in collaboration with industry to work up to 24 kA at sub-ppm accuracy. The paper describes the design and verification.

articleTitle: Superconductor digital-to-analog converter based on processing of SFQ pulses
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Recently we designed and successfully tested a prototype of a superconducting digital-to-analog converter (DAC) based on processing single flux quantum (SFQ) pulses. Two unique features make the device very attractive for metrology applications: (i) The generation of output voltage is based on the fundamentally accurate Josephson frequency-to-voltage relationship. (ii) The device does not require any external signals with frequencies higher than 100 MHz. It is expected that the DAC will be used as a key component of novel standards and calibrators of ac voltage with frequency up to 1 MHz. The implemented prototype has low magnitude of output voltage (about 10 mV) which is far lower than the 1 to 10 V target magnitude.

articleTitle: Level analysis and control of electromagnetic radiation from microwave oscillators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Theoretical and experimental studies of spurious and extra waveguide oscillation in crossed-field devices are described. Theoretically the existence is shown of spurious and extra waveguide oscillations in wide band (from some cycles to dozen gigacycles), and amplitude-from some millivolts to hundred volts. We studied two oscillation processes: ion and electron. Experimentally these oscillations are detected in the output spectrum, and emission from cathode junction is found. Thus crossed-field devices influence EMC.

articleTitle: Determination of the gravitational constant G using a Fabry-Perot pendulum resonator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The gravitational constant G is the least well known fundamental constant. Our unique method of measuring G is described, followed by a report on discovered systematic errors and thereupon realized upgrades to significantly reduce those errors. We will present the first results obtained after the upgrade.

articleTitle: Spectral theory of operators and its application to more accurate evaluation of the velocity of light based on volume and open superconductive resonators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: New mathematical methods are proposed and substantiated for the determination of the velocity of light. The methods are based on impedance measurements of superconductors. Analytical formulas suitable for physical analysis and calculations are produced.

articleTitle: A DVM-based accurate measurement setup for QHE resistance measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper we describe the setup we have developed for intercomparison of resistors with the quantum Hall effect using a 8 1/2 digit digital voltmeter. A unique feature of the system is its simplicity in setup and operation, whereas at the same time an estimated accuracy of better than 1 part in 10/sup 7/ is obtained.

articleTitle: Voltage-burden induced errors in the detection of bridge balance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The influence of voltage burden on the detection of bridge balance may be overlooked as people may simply believe that a null current represents a bridge balance. In this study, the influence is investigated, and the measures for minimising the influence are introduced. A method for determining both the resistance ratio and voltage burden is also proposed.

articleTitle: The quantized Hall resistance standard at CMS
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on precision measurements of the quantum Hall resistance (QHR) in Center for Measurement Standards (CMS) for primary resistance standard establishment. The standard reproduces points of R/sub H/(i=2) and R/sub H/(i=4) with relative uncertainties, given as one-standard-deviation estimates, of 6/spl times/10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: A watt meter standard for the audio frequency range
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A watt meter standard, based on digital sampling, has been designed and evaluated for the audio frequency range. The watt meter is based on two commercially available sampling DVMs. The power spectrum is calculated with DFT analysis. High accuracy is achieved by phase locking and simultaneous sampling.

articleTitle: CCC inductances calculation: validity of the image method
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The inductance of the sensing coil of a cryogenic current comparator differs from its nominal value due to the presence of superconducting structures. The effective inductance can be determined by the "image method" or by an iterative method with help of FEM software. Both procedures are described and their outcomes discussed.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of the atomic mass of /sup 6/Li using a Penning ion trap mass spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A cryogenic (4 K) Penning ion trap mass spectrometer has been used to measure the mass ratios of /sup 6/Li/sup +///sup 12/C/sup 2+/ and /sup 6/Li/sup +//D/sub 3//sup +/ using small numbers of ions (1-10). These measurements result in a value for the atomic mass of /sup 6/Li of 6.015122795(16) u, which has a fractional uncertainty of 2.7/spl times/10/sup -9/, representing a factor of 30 improvement over the published accepted value.

articleTitle: Metrological analysis of a high current measurement system
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper presents a study about a high current measurement system. This system is used to measure a high pulsed current with precision. A metrological analysis was begun to determine the real precision and the limitations of this system. In the first part of the paper, the measurement principle, based on the inductive effect, is presented. In the second part, the metrological process is presented and the reasons of this analysis are explained. The main limitations of this system are described in the third part. These main limitations depend on the current probe positions and the choice of the numerical algorithm used to analyse the recorded electrical signals. Finally, we can measure a six megaamperes pulsed current with a precision of /spl plusmn/5% in using this metrological study and a new calibration of the system.

articleTitle: Progress in the LPTF cesium beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The present short term stability of our optically pumped frequency standard is /spl sigma//sub y/(/spl tau/)=3.8/spl middot/10/sup -13/ /spl tau//sup - 1/2 /. A great deal of work has been performed in order to reduce the uncertainties of this standard. An example is given with two of them, associated to the second order Doppler effect and to the presence of a microwave field outside the Ramsey cavity.

articleTitle: Automatic bridge for comparison of inductances based on difference voltage measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An inductance bridge to compare inductors by 1:1 substitution method is proposed. This bridge is based on difference voltage measurement. Uncertainties of less that 0.01% are possible for inductors from 1 mH to 100 mH at 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Source-pull and multiharmonic load-pull measurements based on six-port techniques
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An original measurement system for nonlinear microwave power transistor characterization, using six-port reflectometers, is presented. It allows independent active tuning of the output impedances at f/sub 0/ and 2f/sub 0/ (multiharmonic load-pull) and variation of the source impedance at the input port at f/sub 0/ (source-pull). Experimental results are shown for a commercial GaAs MESFET power transistor.

articleTitle: Asia/Pacific Metrology Program (APMP) comparison of DC voltage-1996/97
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An APMP international comparison of DC voltage, with 15 participants, using a Zener cell as traveling standard was carried out from February 1996 to December 1997. The final results show an agreement of the majority of participating laboratories of better than 0.2 ppm for 1.018 V output.

articleTitle: Establishing and verifying the Norwegian absolute ACV
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Automatic set-ups for comparison of AC-DC transfer standards and generation of absolute ACV have been developed. The set-ups are controlled by modern Microsoft Windows NT compatible software. The methods used and the set-ups are successfully tested in three international intercomparisons. Results are given.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric transfer difference of thermal converters measured with a Josephson source
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have measured the thermoelectric transfer difference of two thermal voltage converters using a Josephson source and compared the results to similar measurements made with a conventional semiconductor source. Both sources use the fast reversed DC method. The Josephson source is an array of 16 384 superconductor-normal-superconductor Josephson junctions that is rapidly switched between voltage states of +0.5 V, 0 V, and -0.5 V. A marginally significant difference is detected between measurements with the two different sources.

articleTitle: Fabrication of high-value standard resistors
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: NIST has fabricated stable, transportable 10 M/spl Omega/ and 1 G/spl Omega/ standard resistors for use in an international comparison of high resistances. This fabrication process is being applied to the construction of standard resistors of values up to 100 T/spl Omega/, with initial results indicating significant improvements in stability and fewer adverse effects induced by mechanical shock and vibration.

articleTitle: Automated ADC characterisation using the histogram test stimulated by Gaussian noise
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The determination of the stationary transfer function of an ADC using an automated test system and employing the histogram test using, however, Gaussian noise as the stimulus signal, is presented. This transfer function is used to derive merit figures like SNDR, THD and effective number of bits.

articleTitle: Ellipsometric measurements on single-crystal silicon spheres [for Avogadro's constant determination]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Beside other parameters the growth of oxide layers on silicon surfaces depends on the surface preparation and on the crystal orientation. Measurements of the oxide layer thicknesses on silicon spheres are described. The results show a strong dependence on the crystal orientations which may originate from the polishing process. After HF-etching this orientation effect cannot be distinguished anymore.

articleTitle: Low noise single electron transistors of stacked design
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Overlap-type single-electron transistors with the different island to substrate contact areas were studied. We found that background charge noise reduces with the contact area reduction, that clearly indicates to the substrate origin of the noise. For transistors with the smallest contact area with the substrate (stacked configuration), we reached the noise level of 2.5.10/sup -5/ e//spl radic/Hz at 10 Hz, which is the lowest noise figure of SET devices measured so far.

articleTitle: Lasers for a trapped Hg/sup +/ optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have demonstrated a frequency source at 563 nm with an approximately 6 Hz linewidth for use in an optical frequency standard based on trapped and cooled /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ ions. Additionally, we are developing solid state laser replacements for gas and dye lasers presently used for driving 194 nm and 282 nm /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ transitions.

articleTitle: Calibration of dissipation factor standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Dissipation factor (DF) standards obtained by connecting a shielded three-terminal capacitor in series with a shielded resistor have been developed for calibration purposes. An analysis of these DF standards, including precautions in their construction and use, is presented and calibration procedures using the NIST high voltage capacitance bridge is discussed.

articleTitle: A novel measurement technique for microwave frequency translating devices (FTD)
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new measurement setup for the characterization of frequency translating devices (FTD) is presented. The proposed approach allows one-step full characterization of FTDs by measuring both the magnitudes and phases of the incident and reflected waves at all signal ports. The application of the proposed approach to the characterization of a double balanced mixer is presented.

articleTitle: A high-frequency thermal power comparator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new thermal power comparator (TPC) is described that covers a frequency range from power frequencies to 200 kHz. The TPC features a resistive voltage divider and shunts, and a thermal multiplier with two differential high-impedance inputs. It incorporates novel developments in the method of reducing LF and HF errors in the power comparison.

articleTitle: Emulation of three terminal standard inductors with tee networks
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper we propose a technique for emulating three terminal standard inductors with a tee network of two resistors and a capacitor. By separate measurement of the resistances and the capacitance, the equivalent inductance may be calculated. By introducing unloading amplifiers into the emulation tee network, unwanted impedances to ground may be cancelled. Using this approach we anticipate that inductors in the range 100 mH to 10 H may be emulated to an accuracy of at least 100 parts per million.

articleTitle: Programmable 1 volt DC voltage standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have developed a Josephson voltage standard that produces intrinsically stable voltages that are programmable from -1.1 V to +1.1 V. The standard uses a binary array sequence of 32,768 SNS (superconductor-normal-superconductor) Josephson junctions. The output can source or sink up to 2 mA and thus has high noise immunity.

articleTitle: Accuracy evaluation of the optically pumped Cs frequency standard at NRLM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: To evaluate the accuracy of the optically pumped Cs frequency standard at NRLM (NRLM-4), we measured its frequency stability and the frequency difference between NRLM-4 and the international atomic time (TAI).

articleTitle: Improved studies on an HTS current cryocomparator with thick-film YBCO toroidal shield
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Investigation are continuing on a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) having the shield made by an extended thick film of the YBCO high-temperature superconductor (HTS). Recent results relate to the adopted open-toroidal open-tube geometry are reported, regarding both error ratio attenuation measurements and numerical treatment of a mathematical model.

articleTitle: Micromechanical silicon scale
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A novel miniature capacitive scale is described. The device is realized by micromachining single-crystalline silicon. Our design calculations show that it is possible to weigh one gram with an accuracy on the order of a part in million.

articleTitle: Two international comparisons of SMU 10 V Josephson array voltage standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Interlaboratory comparisons of the SMU 10 V voltage standard based on Josephson effect have been carried out with the BNM/LCIE and the NPL 10 V Josephson standards. The comparison method was indirect using Zener diode references as the travelling standards. The results show agreement between the SMU and the BNM/LCIE calibrations of the Fluke 732 A reference standard 23.5 nV and between the SMU and the NPL calibrations of the Fluke 732 B 55 nV.

articleTitle: Calibration comparison for vector network analyzers with switching errors
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. This paper demonstrates a method for comparing vector network analyzer calibrations in which each parameter in the error model, including the switch terms, may vary. This extends earlier calibration comparison methods that assume the switch terms to be fixed. The method is therefore applicable even to common methods that do not measure the switch terms directly and may therefore determine them erroneously.

articleTitle: AC and DC voltage source using quantized pulses
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have developed an accurate synthesized voltage source for AC and DC metrology, based on the quantized pulses of Josephson junctions. We demonstrated this technique in experiments with arrays of junctions clocked at 6 Gbit/s and synthesized sine waves with millivolt amplitudes at frequencies up to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: CCE intercomparison of AC-DC voltage transfer standards at high frequencies (1-50 MHz)
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: From August 1995 until January 1998, the intercomparison of AC-DC voltage transfer standards at high frequencies has been carried out. Two travel standards have been measured by 15 national standard institutes. The preliminary results in the frequency range from 1 to 50 MHz show a good agreement between the majority of participants.

articleTitle: A proposal for a new moving-coil experiment
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new type of moving-coil watt balance is under construction at the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology (OFMET). The aim of the experiment is the monitoring of the kilogram by means of the electrical standards with a relative uncertainty of /spl les/10/sup -8/. The paper presents the main features of the proposed instrument.

articleTitle: The optical calcium frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: PTB operates an optical wavelength/frequency standard by stabilizing the frequency of a laser to the intercombination transition /sup 3/P/sub 1/-/sup 1/S/sub 0/ of atomic /sup 40/Ca at /spl lambda//spl cong/657 nm. The relative uncertainty of the standard has been reduced by the use of laser cooled atoms and by measurements of the optical frequency to below 2.5/spl middot/10(-13).

articleTitle: Traceability and uncertainty of field-strength measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new electromagnetic field-strength standard generator up to 1 GHz has been set up at PTB by means of a /spl mu/TEM-cell (septum-height 35 mm), a field-sensor transfer-standard, and a GTEM-cell as working standard for calibrations and EMC-testing, to guarantee traceability of field-strength measurement to the basic SI-units including uncertainty figures.

articleTitle: Calibration of precision measuring amplifiers for strain gauge transducers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A method is described that utilizes a ratio device consisting of multi-decade inductive voltage dividers to calibrate precision measuring amplifiers for strain gauge transducers. Most frequently, this device is used to calibrate 2.5 mV/V ranges of the amplifiers, relative standard uncertainty being 5 ppm for the ratio of 0.0025 and at 225 Hz.

articleTitle: Low frequency stochastic true RMS instrument
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A stochastic instrument for true RMS measurement in the low-frequency range is presented. Variably accuracy is achieved by varying the measuring time of the instrument. Accuracy of 0.2% FS is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of a 10 mH inductance standard between UME-PTB
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Turkish and German Metrology Institutes (UME and PTB) performed an intercomparison of 10 mH inductance standards at 1 kHz. The measurements of the thermostatically-controlled transfer standard of PTB were taken by new Maxwell-Wien bridge with a Wagner arm made in UME. Relative difference of UME and PTB measurements on the same standard was found to be 5.10/sup -6/. Results have shown that this type of Maxwell-Wien bridge is capable of producing very precise measurements on standard inductors and promised further developments that will increase the accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Extension of voltage range for power and energy calibrations
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A special purpose ac voltage divider system having voltage ratios of 600 V, 480 V, 360 V, and 240 V to 120 V has been developed to extend the voltage range of primary electric power calibrations from 120 volts to 600 volts at power frequencies of 50 and 60 Hz. The system consists of a special two-stage resistive divider compensated with an active circuit, thereby reducing the error contributions to below 1 /spl mu/V/V. The developmental goal to realize ac voltage scaling within 5 /spl mu/V/V uncertainty in a device verifiable with dc resistance ratio measurements has been attained.

articleTitle: Hysteretic and reversible anomalies of resistance alloys
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: At highest level of precision most standard resistors show anomalies in their resistance value if they are exposed to changes in ambient temperature, i.e. the resistance depends hysteretically on temperature. This hysteretical behaviour was found not to be random but reproducible. We report on experimental results showing this effect and outline a possible physical explanation.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of frequency-doubled Nd:YAG lasers at 532 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report the preliminary results on the frequency stabilization of two frequency-doubled diode-pumped Nd:YAG lasers to hyperfine structure components of the rovibrational transition P(54)32-0 of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ with the sub-Doppler sidebands method. In a preliminary experiment, we have obtained a relative frequency stability of 2.9/spl middot/10/sup -13/ for an integration time of 1 s.

articleTitle: Stabilization and frequency measurement of the I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report improved stabilization results for and a more accurate frequency measurement of the 532 nm iodine-stabilized system based on a frequency-doubled Nd:YAG ring laser.

articleTitle: A system for the measurement of complex voltage ratios at industrial frequencies
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A system for the measurement of complex voltage ratios has been set up. It consists of two synchronised sampling voltmeters and a suitable software program that performs the acquisition and the determination of the two voltages and the phase difference. The results show that the system can be satisfactorily used in many types of precision measurement at industrial frequency.

articleTitle: Estimation of capacitance of small junction from liquid He temperature measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We show the way to estimate capacitance C and tunnel resistance R/sub T/ of a small junction from 4.2 K measurements using high temperature expansion for I-V curve. It enables us prompt feedback to fabricate the single electron tunneling elements.

articleTitle: Calorimetric thermal voltage converter as a wideband calculable standard of ac-dc difference
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A calorimetric thermal voltage converter is used at the National Research Council of Canada as a high-frequency reference standard of the ac-dc difference. This paper describes its redesigned realization. Calculations and test results in the 10 Hz-100 MHz frequency range are shown.

articleTitle: A new approach to the design of wide-band multiprobe reflectometers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new design approach for low-cost multiprobe reflectometers is presented. While traditional circuits adopt equally-spaced probes, the presented solution provide a method to greatly enhance the bandwidth of the measuring system by a proper choice of each probe position. As example, a five-probe 0.6-16 GHz system has been designed.

articleTitle: Determination of the Tesla-to-ampere ratio by modified electromagnetic method for /spl gamma/'p-measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Tesla-to-amper ratio giving the biggest error in /spl gamma/'p-low-field-experiment was determined using modified non-contacting method. Total error of 0.164 ppm was attained. Solenoid constant and /spl gamma/'p-value were corrected on magnetic susceptibility of air. The result is /spl gamma/'p=2.67515418 10/sup 8/ s/sup -1/ T/sup -1/ (Tesla BI-90) with total uncertainty of 0.18 ppm.

articleTitle: Measurement of reflection coefficient of RF sources-and associated uncertainty
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The measurement of VRC of a generator is presented. The "ripple technique" is used, with an air line, a directional bridge and a short. An uncertainty model is given which takes into account unwanted signals (directivity and test port match). Finally, the results are presented along with the estimated uncertainty.

articleTitle: Josephson series array voltage standard at National Physical Laboratory, India
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A voltage standard system based an the Josephson series array to represent the volt at National Physical Laboratory (NPL), India has been recently established. This paper describes the measurement set up at 1 volt level and the results that has been obtained in calibrating the secondary standard.

articleTitle: Microwave resonant cavity measurements for determining proportions of coal and limestone in powdered mixtures
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Microwave resonant cavity measurements on mixtures of pulverized coal and limestone show that the proportions of the two components can be determined from the ratio of the resonant frequency shift and the change in the transmission factor when mixed coal and limestone samples are inserted into the cavity.

articleTitle: Josephson arrays at 70 GHz for conventional and programmable voltage standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes the performance under real calibration conditions of improved conventional Nb/Al/AlO/sub x//Nb (SIS) 10-V Josephson series arrays (JJAs) fabricated in the last two years at PTB. A new type of Nb/Al/AlO/sub x//Al/AlO/sub x//Al/Nb (SINIS) array is described which is useful for programmable voltage standards in the frequency range from 70 GHz to 90 GHz.

articleTitle: Progress towards an atomic fountain frequency standard at PTB
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The scheme of an atomic fountain frequency standard which is under construction at PTB is explained in some detail and first results are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Pressure coefficients of some Zener-diode based electronic voltage standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present results of a systematic study of the pressure dependence of the 1.018 V and 10 V outputs of fifteen Fluke 732B electronic voltage standards. Fourteen have relative pressure coefficients near 1.9 parts in 10/sup 9//hPa but one has coefficients an order of magnitude smaller and of the opposite sign. Pressure dependence can produce significant errors in all instruments studied.

articleTitle: Improvements of NRLM superconducting magnetic levitation system for absolute determination of /spl Phi//sub 0/
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The NRLM superconducting magnetic levitation system is now refining for the determination of Magnetic Flux Quantum /spl Phi//sub 0/ with small 25 g mass floating body. Recent study to investigate error sources and improvements are described in this paper.

articleTitle: A precision contactless trajectory control for moving-element electrometric systems
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Virtual constraints acting like contactless guides are obtained using eccentricity transducers and electrostatic actuators designed for cylindrical geometry. The experimental study is finalized to avoid instability in electrometric systems for absolute measurements that involve the kinematics of the moving element. A nearly nanometric resolution and a two orders of magnitude reduction of the displacement from the assigned trajectory are presented as interim results.

articleTitle: Electro-optic probing of microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present an S-parameter measurement system based on electro-optic sampling for the on-wafer testing of microwave integrated circuits. The advantages of non-invasive electro-optic testing over conventional network analyser systems are discussed for passive, active and analogue circuits up to 20 GHz. The measurement procedures, repeatability and uncertainty in measurements are reported.

articleTitle: Compact frequency standard at 192.6 THz (1556 nm) based on the 5S-5D two-photon transition in rubidium at 778 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present our recent results toward the realization of an absolute frequency standard at 1556 nm based on the two-photon transition in rubidium at 778 nm. A compact transportable absolute frequency standard is described. Emphasis is put on the design of a periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide for efficient second-harmonic generation.

articleTitle: Assessment of field uniformity in a GTEM cell using a novel non-invasive scanning positioning system
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. To assess field uniformity within a GTEM cell, a set of field strength measurements have to be made over a 3D mesh of points inside the cell. To minimise the disturbance of the field structure during the measurement of the probe, its support and the scanning system should be minimally perturbing. The problem of how to repeatedly position the probe element in space without disturbing the field has presented a significant challenge. The requirements of the positioning system are that the probe can move in all three dimensions, over a reasonably large volume, preferably near to the testing zone in the GTEM and under computer control. NPL has developed a novel automated positioning system consisting of a platform supported at its four corners by strings running to a set of motors mounted outside of the cell. Connected to each motor drive is a drum around which the strings are would and by winding in or out certain lengths of string it is possible to move the platform around in three dimensions. The exact angular rotation required by each motor to obtain a given position in space is calculated by a computer program and implemented under IEEE bus control. This program is also used to coordinate the data acquisition from whichever field detection system is used.

articleTitle: Proposed strategies for time and frequency traceability in the Southern African Development Community
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The newly established metrology infrastructure for the Southern African Development Community, called SADCMET, has highlighted the need for an in-depth study of the metrology facilities available in the Southern African region. This paper deals with the proposed strategies for determining the capabilities in the region focusing on time and frequency.

articleTitle: A traceability of loss angle standards at KRISS
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A traceability of the loss angle standards at low frequencies has been established at KRISS by a joint work with VNIIM. The loss angle of the related standards and bridges can be measured and calibrated in the range of from 1/spl times/10/sup -6/ rad to /spl pi//4 rad with uncertainty of from 5/spl times/10/sup -7/ to 5/spl times/10/sup -4/ at frequencies 100 Hz to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: The quantum roulette noise thermometer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A novel form of primary thermometer called the quantum roulette noise thermometer (QRNT), based on flux quantisation in a HTS superconducting ring, has been proposed. The basis of the QRNT is that the flux state of a SQUID ring is allowed to evolve freely. The flux state is repeatedly interrogated to establish a probability distribution from which the temperature of the device is derived.

articleTitle: NIST cesium fountain frequency standard: preliminary results
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have designed and constructed a laser-cooled cesium fountain for use as a primary frequency standard. This standard incorporates several unique design features, including a method for mapping the C-field region, a second microwave cavity for use in state preparation and a cavity design with extremely low distributed cavity phase shift. Preliminary results of the evaluation and performance of this device will be discussed, including several novel design features.

articleTitle: Status of SET activities at NMi-VSL
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We discuss the present status of the activities at the NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium in the field of application of single electron transport devices in a future primary standard of electrical current. The activities cover single electron transport (SET) device fabrication and testing, as well as precision measurements of the small SET currents.

articleTitle: Second order in mass ratio radiative-recoil corrections to hyperfine splitting in muonium
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Radiative-recoil corrections to hyperfine splitting in muonium of order /spl alpha/(Z/spl alpha/)(m/M)/sup 2/E/sub F/ and of order (Z/sup 2//spl alpha/)(Z/spl alpha/)(m/M)/sup 2/E/sub F/ are calculated. An analytic expression [(-61n2-4/3)/spl alpha/(Z/spl alpha/)-12/17(Z/sup 2//spl alpha/)(Z/spl alpha/)](M/m)/sup 2/E/sub F/ is obtained. Numerically the correction is equal to -0.0351 kHz and is of the same order of magnitude as the planned accuracy of the experiment on measuring the hyperfine splitting which is now running at Los Alamos.

articleTitle: A method for precise RMS measurements of periodic signals at low frequencies
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new method of precision reconstruction and the RMS measurements of the low frequency signals is presented. The method is based on the reconstruction technique and additionally uses a precise measurement of the rectified signal average (RSA). This approach considerably increases accuracy of the RMS measurement.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurements and intercomparisons of He-Ne/CH/sup 4/ (/spl lambda/=3.39 /spl mu/m), CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ (/spl lambda/=10.6 /spl mu/m) frequency stabilized lasers and Cs primary standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Results of absolute frequency calibration of the He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ transportable optical frequency standard (TOFS) and intercomparisons of the TOFS with CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ OFS carried out on 1996-1997 by a collaboration of three organizations (Lebedev Institute, PTB, and BNM-LPTF) are reported.

articleTitle: Experimental noise sources in the NIST watt balance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The present NIST watt balance has relative combined standard uncertainty of about 145 nW/W. The final results of this phase of the experiment are presented. Improvements in the Type B (nonstatistical) uncertainty contributions, along with several correction factors and noise sources, are also discussed.

articleTitle: An automated measurement system for core loss characterization
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An automated measurement system for core loss characterization under sine wave or square wave excitation is described. This system can accomplish these aims within specified magnetic induction and frequency ranges and at different temperatures with high accuracy, thanks to the techniques used in the acquisition and computation of the waveforms involved in loss calculation.

articleTitle: A determination of Newton's gravitational constant using the MSL torsion balance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. We will describe the results of a new determination of the Newtonian gravitational constant (G) made since our last value reported at the 1994 CPEM. At the 1996 CEPM we reported a number of difficulties in completing the measurement in progress at that time. We have now solved all of these problems and at the time of writing believe that we will be in a position to report an improved value of G. The paper will briefly report the differences in the measurement since the last CPEM and present our latest result and its uncertainty.

articleTitle: The UWA/PTB optical to microwave frequency chain
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper reports on the development of a second generation coherent optical to microwave frequency chain based on the difference frequency domain method. We will report the chain design as well as presenting measurements of the performance of the critical elements: efficient nonlinear radiation production and laser diode phase locking.

articleTitle: On accuracy of Lamb shift measurements in hydrogen
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Detailed analysis of systematic errors in measurements of Lamb shift in hydrogen by the atomic interferometer method is presented. The experimental results are compared with high-precision theoretical data.

articleTitle: Atmospheric inhomogeneities effects on microwave distance measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This work aims to define the tropospheric turbulence effects on a high precision distance measurement radar. The signal is characterised statistically to compute the final accuracy of the instrument. Moreover, compensation techniques are suggested.

articleTitle: Measurement system for sound velocity in positive magnetostrictive amorphous wires
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A measurement system for sound velocity, based on the magnetostrictive delay lines, is presented. Experimental results are reported concerning the dependence of the longitudinal sound velocity in positive magnetostrictive amorphous wires on the tensile stress and bias magnetic field magnitudes.

articleTitle: Improved interferometric method to measure near-carrier AM and PM noise
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An improved version of the interferometric method to measure near-carrier AM and PM noise is being presented. The main feature of this scheme is its capability to reduce the instrument noise by correlating the output of two equal interferometers, thus enhancing the sensitivity. The method, microwave band implementation and experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of the 2/sup 3/P/sub 0/-2/sup 3/P/sub 1/ helium fine structure interval
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper we describe a measurement of the helium 2/sup 3/P/sub 0/-/sup 2/3P/sub 1/ interval, obtained from a full optical approach in an atomic beam of metastable He. Direct frequency determination and control of systematic effects leads to an accuracy of 3 kHz. By comparison with a precise atomic theory, a 50 ppb accurate determination of the fine structure constant /spl alpha/ will be possible.

articleTitle: Interference effects on the spectroscopic measurement of radiation temperature
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An earlier work investigation of a photodiode spectroscopic system for radiation temperature measurements has revealed interference patterns in the radiometric data. This work will report the results of radiometric measurements, demonstrate the interference effects, investigate their origin and discuss the uncertainty introduced to the temperature determined due to the interference fringes.

articleTitle: Fabrication of quantum Hall devices for low magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The quantized Hall resistance of a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in AlGaAs/GaAs heterostructures is used for the realization of the unit of resistance. With respect to an application in magnets with lower fields, we have produced such devices with carrier concentrations even below 3/spl middot/10/sup 15/ m/sup -2/ and checked their metrological quality.

articleTitle: The molar volume of silicon: discrepancies and limitations
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new representation of the current molar volume discrepancy is offered which attends to a previous incorrect account of early NBS work. First non-null test results are presented from comparisons of discrepant samples. A discussion of intrinsic limitations of melt grown crystals is included.

articleTitle: Determination of G by means of a beam balance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. We are preparing a high-precision measurement of the gravitational constant G, using a new technique. Test measurements with water as field masses have been done and G has been determined with an uncertainty of 240 ppm. In the next step 13.5 tons of mercury will be used as field masses.

articleTitle: Higher-order binding corrections to the Lamb shift
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper reports the status and progress regarding the evaluation of higher order binding corrections to the Lamb shift in systems with low nuclear charge Z. Recently, the evaluation of all binding corrections to the Lamb shift of nP states in hydrogenlike systems at low Z up to the order of /spl alpha//sup 7/ (n=2,3,4) has been completed. Using an extrapolation of numerical results, it is possible to obtain an approximate value for higher-order corrections to excited S-states also. Moreover, a calculation is in progress whose ultimate goal is to eliminate any error from low-Z type series expansions or extrapolations of numerical data for high Z. This calculation involves the use of convergence acceleration techniques for certain hypergeometric series and takes advantage of the NIST SGT POWER ONYX and IBM SP/2 supercomputing facilities.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of iodine-stabilized 543 nm He-Ne laser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present our work on the frequency measurement of iodine-stabilized 543 nm He-Ne laser. We have finished the following experiment: compact iodine-stabilized 543 nm He-Ne laser and cavity enhanced second harmonic generation of CO/sub 2/ laser. We are preparing the final frequency measurement, and the results will be presented.

articleTitle: A microwave interferometer system for humidity measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A microwave interferometer system for humidity measurement has been developed. The system is based on the sensitivity of the air permittivity to the water vapor content and offers a faster response and a better air pollution insensitivity with respect to the traditional humidity sensors which are based on hygroscopic substances. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the new approach in the range of 20% RH to 70% RH.

articleTitle: Inter-laboratory comparison of high direct voltage resistance dividers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A 150 kV NML divider was used as a travelling standard in comparison tests against standard dividers maintained at KRISS of Korea and NRC of Canada. Useful results in terms of the relative ratio changes among the dividers under high voltages were obtained. The comparison tests were shown to be especially valuable for evaluating the ratio drifts of the dividers due to prolonged application of high voltage.

articleTitle: Low permeability reference standards with improved high magnetic field strength performance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Commercial instruments for determining the relative magnetic permeability of weakly magnetic materials require traceable calibration. This is achieved using reference standards of known permeability. These materials suffer to some extent from the fact that their relative magnetic permeability varies with the applied magnetic field strength. When used to calibrate instruments, this can introduce significant errors. We will report the development of a material which improves this situation. By uniformly dispersing iron particles in an acrylic matrix their self demagnetized properties are substantially retained and consequently the permeability changes with applied field are significantly smaller than for conventional materials.

articleTitle: A new current-comparator-based high-voltage low-power-factor wattmeter
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A current-comparator technique is applied to power measurements for obtaining a highly accurate high-voltage low-power-factor wattmeter. The instrument has two time-division-multiplier-type wattmeters. One wattmeter, in conjunction with a microcontroller, is used to provide automatic balancing of the quadrature component of the load current in a current comparator against a quadrature current from a current-comparator-based high-voltage quadrature reference source. The other wattmeter is used to measure the residual loss component of the load current. This new current-comparator-based high-voltage low-power-factor wattmeter has an order of magnitude improvement in accuracy and a lower measuring range in power factor than a previously developed instrument. It has an estimated uncertainty with respect to its readings of less than 0.25 percent at 0.01 power factor and higher, 0.5 percent at 0.001 power factor, and 5 percent at 0.0001 power factor.

articleTitle: Distortion of fluorescence line profile due to laser radiation pressure in an RF trap
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Distortion of laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) spectral line profile of trapped Mg ions in an RF trap is observed and analyzed. It is found by establishing a theoretical model that collisions and laser radiation pressure induce the distortion. Furthermore, a new type line profile predicted by this model is observed.

articleTitle: Zero-current voltage oscillations and non-linear transport in Quantum Hall GaAs-AlGaAs heterostructures
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Zero-current voltage oscillations in Quantum Hall samples have been reported in literature. Its origin is not yet understood. Here we propose a possible explanation based on a thermoelectric effect caused by noise input and local differences in the carrier density near the voltage contacts. Experiments on non-linear transport in GaAs-AlGaAs heterostructures are presented.

articleTitle: Sub-kilohertz optical spectroscopy by time domain atom interferometry
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A time domain atom interferometer is used to compare the frequency of the Mg intercombination transition at 457 nm with an optical oscillator with sub-kHz resolution. An estimated accuracy of 2·10/sup -15/ is achieved with laser cooled and trapped atoms. The resolved line Q-factor is better than 10/sup 12/.

articleTitle: Improved AC quantized Hall measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: AC quantized Hall resistance (QHR) measurements have been performed with an improved probe and sample mounting system. We describe investigations of the structure of the R/sub H/ plateau versus frequency, sample configuration, sample current and temperature. We have observed R/sub xx/ minima smaller than 0.02 ppm of R/sub H/.

articleTitle: Instrumental delay calibration for VLBI time comparison via short baseline interferometry
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have developed a short baseline interferometry (SBI) system with a directly controlled reference frequency for VLBI time comparison. SBI is a kind of portable clock method in order to calibrate the instrumental delay. Instrumental delay is an important factor in determining the accuracy of time-and-frequency comparisons.

articleTitle: All-diode-laser based, dual-cavity AgGaS/sub 2/ difference-frequency spectrometer for the 9-11 /spl mu/m range
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on preliminary performance of a mid-IR doubly-resonant difference frequency (DFG) spectrometer generating 30 nW of 10.2-/spl mu/m tunable radiation out of 7 mW and 275 mW of the diode laser pump inputs at 778 nm and 842 nm.

articleTitle: PTB-UME intercomparison with 100 M/spl Omega/ resistors using Wheatstone bridge method
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An intercomparison of 100 M/spl Omega/ Guildline 9330 resistance standards was carried out. The standards were first measured at UME using both an MI 6000A bridge and Wheatstone bridge voltage detection method. The resistors were then measured at PTB using an MI 6000A bridge and then again at UME. The results of these intercomparisons are presented.

articleTitle: A first attempt to realize (multiple-QHE devices)-series array resistance standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper shows that the possibility exists to fabricate a single chip of 7.5/spl times/5.5 mm/sup 2/ composed of several QHE devices having the same density and mobility. Metrological characteristics of some samples with devices placed in series are described.

articleTitle: High accuracy, high frequency power multimeter MF100
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A high accuracy, high bandwidth electric power measurement system is described achieving a accuracy better than 10/sup -3/ on the input signal frequencies up to 100 kHz. This is the result of a new design with full integration of improved analogue solutions and high speed digital and computational techniques.

articleTitle: Frequency measurement of the 2S-12D transitions in hydrogen and deuterium. New determination of the Rydberg constant
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have performed the first pure frequency measurement of the 2S-12D two-photon transitions in atomic hydrogen and deuterium. These frequencies are compared to two optical standards, the CO/sub 2/ laser stabilized on the OsO/sub 4/ molecule and the optical rubidium laser standard (LD/Rb) (namely a laser diode at 778 nm stabilized on the 5S/sub 1/2/-5D/sub 5/2/ two-photon transition of rubidium). We have built a frequency chain to connect the hydrogen lines to the frequency standards. The main part of the experiment is located in the LKB laboratory, one part of the frequency chain is in the LPTF laboratory, two optical fibers linked the two parts of this experiment.

articleTitle: Calibration of high voltage transformers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The calibration of the current comparator which forms the main part of the system is also described.

articleTitle: Study of SET devices for metrological applications at 0.4 K
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Single electron effects have been observed in devices measured at temperatures as low as 0.4 K. The charge noise was measured in electrometers and evidence of background charge fluctuations was observed. Custom-made micro-coax cables have also been fabricated and their measured attenuation is found to increase with the 3/4'th power of frequency, in contrast to the 1/2 power dependence expected from the theory.

articleTitle: Maintenance and validation of a resistance ratio chain for platinum resistance thermometry
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A simple method for establishing a resistance ratio chain used in precision resistance thermometry is described. The chain consists of a group of AC resistance standards, maintained with known resistance ratios, to span a range of thermometer resistance ratios from 0.00119 to 1.0 as required for platinum resistance thermometry between 13.8033 K and 273.16 K.

articleTitle: A QHE system based on a Josephson potentiometer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A measuring system of resistance standards based on the QHE has been developed at Centro Espanol de Metrologia (CEM) using the Josephson Array Voltage Standard (JAVS) as potentiometer. The results obtained with this method have an uncertainty of 1 part in 10/sup 8/.

articleTitle: Measurements of the AC longitudinal resistance of a GaAs-AlGaAs quantum Hall device
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Measurements of the AC longitudinal resistance R/sub x/ of a quantum Hall device have been carried out at frequencies from 160 Hz to 16 kHz, with an improved measuring system and a new procedure for rejecting the quadrature component due to stray capacitance. The results show a linear dependence on frequency and an asymmetric shape of the R/sub x/ minimum versus magnetic induction.

articleTitle: Results from a detailed calculation of the sensitivity of a cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A detailed calculation of the sensitivity of a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) has been completed. The model accounts for the current distribution on the closed external shield and the overlapped shield around the windings. Additional refinements to the model lead to excellent agreement with sensitivity measurements for a range of CCC geometries.

articleTitle: Direct measurement of standard cells with a Josephson junction array voltage standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The dynamic parameters of standard cells in a circuit for the direct measurement of a standard cell with a Josephson junction array voltage standard were analysed.
