The parameters of the models of a null-detector and a standard cell were experimentally determined. It was found that it is possible to directly measure a standard cell with a voltage standard, with an uncertainty of about 0.001 ppm.

articleTitle: Status of the BNL muon (g-2) experiment
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The muon (g-2) experiment at Brookhaven has completed a first run. The main components of the experiment, which include the superconducting inflector, the superferric storage ring, the electrostatic quadrupoles and the lead-scintillating fiber electron calorimeters, have been commissioned satisfactorily. The analysis of data taken in June and July 1997 is in progress.

articleTitle: Hybrid laser system at 633 nm for length/optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. For the purpose of improving the performance of iodine stabilized He-Ne lasers at 633 nm, we are developing hybrid laser systems, which consist of a He-Ne laser and a visible diode laser. An accuracy of 10/sup -12/ level is aimed.

articleTitle: DC 10:1 Hamon divider with cryogenic contacts
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A study on a DC Hamon divider with superconducting contacts (cryo-contacts Hamon divider) is described. The contact resistance error of the switch had been one of the most significant error sources in the conventional Hamon divider. A specially designed cryogenic switch made of Pb was used at liquid helium temperature for a series-parallel connection of the Hamon resistors which form the upper arm of a Wheatstone bridge for a self calibration. The 10:1 ratio uncertainty of the preliminary measurement is expected to easily reach a 0.1 ppm level.

articleTitle: A three-way, on-site comparison of the 10 V-Josephson voltage standards of the PTB, the SP and the BIPM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Comparisons of the 10 V Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) of the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM) were made at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesansalt (PTB), Braunschweig, Germany with those of the PTB and of the Swedish National Testing and Research Institute (SP), Boras, Sweden, in January 1998. Although the results agree within an overall uncertainty of less than 1 part in 10/sup 9/, a small, but interesting, dependence on microwave power was observed in the DC output of one array.

articleTitle: Rapid and stable measurement of aperiodic phase shift of fiber-optic interferometer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper reports a new technique for measuring aperiodic phase shift induced in the fiber-optic interferometer. The readout can be determined by analyzing four harmonic components of the output of the photodetector without necessity of knowing the Bessel function value, optical source intensity and fringe contrast.

articleTitle: A cryogenic current comparator bridge for resistance measurements at currents of up to 100 A
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The use of cryogenic current comparators at NPL has been limited so far to currents of 100 mA. A new current comparator with a maximum current capacity of 100 A has been developed and will form the basis of a resistance ratio bridge for low value resistors with a relative uncertainty of 10/sup -7/ or better.

articleTitle: Generalized kernels for reconstructing bandlimited functions and their Hilbert transform
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper introduces generalized kernels to be used with the algorithm for reconstructing bandlimited functions from nonequidistant samples which was previously proposed by the authors. The new kernels turn out to be much more compatible with the requirements of numerical implementation, because they lead to matrices with a significantly reduced condition.

articleTitle: The 10 volt fixed frequency Josephson voltage standard at UME-Ulusal Metroloji Enstitusu
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The 10 Volt fixed frequency Josephson voltage standard (FFJVS) at UME, Turkey is described. The FFJVS is based on the PTB designed Josephson junction array and works with a fixed frequency phase-locked Gunn oscillator using a rubidium clock reference. The system is consisted with the national volt of Turkey with a relative uncertainty of 8/spl times/10/sup -9/ at 10 Volt.

articleTitle: The high-precision measure of length for range-finding on the base of electromagnetic radiation
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The wave measure of length on the base of superposition of two electromagnetic monochromatic oscillations having different frequencies is proposed for increasing the precision of the lengths, which are more than 100 m, measurements. The introduction of such measure of length into the metrological practice will permit to realize the structure of metrological assurance of linear measurements on the new conceptual base which assure not only increase of large lengths measurement precision, but also the direct connection with the primary standard of the unit of length.

articleTitle: High-resolution monitoring of air density with an optical wavelength refractometer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A laser optical wavelength refractometer, based on a Michelson interferometer, is used for gas density determination of air as needed for buoyancy corrections in precision weighings. Comparisons are made with other gas density methods, for example the weighing of sinkers. A laser interferometer with an increased optical path resolution of /spl lambda//400 at 633 nm is employed to monitor density changes at the 10/sup 5/ level.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh resolution DC magnetic field measurements using microfabricated fluxgate sensor chips
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this work an innovative fluxgate magnetic sensor chip has been fabricated and successfully tested. This sensor has a wide operation range and ultrahigh sensitivity of 1400 VT/sup -1/. Wide range frequency drive can be used and the linearity of the output signal is demonstrated for (-120 /spl mu/Telsa)-(+120 /spl mu/Telsa) field range.

articleTitle: High-precision imaging interferometer for short gauge blocks
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Interferometric image-analyzing comparator for short gauge blocks is reported. Sophisticated image acquisition and processing software that supports 0.1 nm (/spl lambda//6000) resolution in central length and 1 nm in 3D measurements is developed. Best stability achieved is about 10/sup -9/. Inclination error is minimized and can be measured at 8/spl times/10/sup -9/ uncertainty or better.

articleTitle: An algorithm for the least-squares adjustment enabling objective detection and rejection of discrepant items. II
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new algorithm for the adjustment of fundamental constants presented at CPEM '96 is ameliorated. Rules for selection of the final solutions are established. Final solutions are obtained by excluding the discrepant items one by one and terminating when three criteria for exclusion are satisfied. Our results are compared with the existing recommended values.

articleTitle: Wide band measurement of precision magnetic potentiometer with proportion-integral-differentiator for heavy pulse current
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A wide band measurement system of magnetic potentiometer of high precision with proportion-integral-differentiator for heavy pulse and alternating current is developed. The experiment results show that the new measurement system achieves band spread from 8 kHz to 70 kHz. The band of new measurement system is about 10 times wider than a conventional measurement system. The design and calculations of the new measurement system are given.

articleTitle: Quartz sensor for dielectric measurement in glass-fiber resins
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The dielectric sensor using the sensitive capacitive-dependent crystal is described. In addition, the new idea of excitation of the entire dielectric sensor with stochastic test signals and the dielectric surface-measuring method are given. It includes the influence of test signals on the weighting function uncertainty and on the A/D-D/A conversion. The results of the water absorption measurement in glass-fiber resins are shown experimentally. The uncertainty of the surface dielectric measurement is less than 0.2% (T=15-25/spl deg/C).

articleTitle: An AC voltage standard based on a 1-bit DAC
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The principle of digitally synthesised AC voltage standards is well established. This paper describes a new AC voltage standard which uses a traceable DC voltage standard as an input and produces an AC output at an equivalent r.m.s. voltage to 1 ppm uncertainty. The system works using digital synthesis with a so called 1-bit digital to analogue convertor (DAC).

articleTitle: A calibration technique for the dual six-port automatic network analyzer of sexed test ports
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes a calibration technique for the dual six-port automatic network analyzer which has different sexed connectors on the test ports. It is based on the thru-reflect-line (TRL) technique, and can give some redundancies in calibration procedure and calibration constants for any combination of the test ports.

articleTitle: New developments of rf and microwave power standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The first part of the paper gives an introduction to the modern methods of rf power measurement, including the problems arising when this quantity is disseminated to calibration laboratories. In the second part, new PTB developments of coaxial and waveguide thin-film bolometer power standards in the rf and microwave range are presented.

articleTitle: Realization of the triple points of the International Temperature Scale of 1990 below 84 K at the National Research Council of Canada
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In the temperature region from 13.8 K to 83.8 K, the International Temperature Scale of 1990 (ITS-90) defines a set of thermodynamic fixed points which are used to calibrate an interpolating instrument which then carries the scale for use in the laboratory. The NRC realization of this portion of the ITS-90 will be discussed, with particular attention paid to the cryostat design and the quality of the triple point measurements.

articleTitle: Vertical displacement determination in the NRLM superconducting magnetic levitation system
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The vertical displacement of the gravity center of the floating body is estimated by solving energy equations. To calculate it, all the six degrees of freedom of the floating body are measured by using a optical measurement system.

articleTitle: Subnanometer precision in gauge block measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An interferometric comparator, featuring subnanometer reproducibility and resolution 10/sup -9/, is reported. A set of experiments is proposed for accurate measurements of corrections for interferometer optics and base plate flatness deviations, as well as for roughness of a block and a plate. A length decrease of 0.2 nm due to cleaning procedure of the block before wringing is detected.

articleTitle: Proposed pressure standard based on capacitance measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We propose to measure the dielectric constant /spl epsiv/ and the thermodynamic temperature T of helium near 273.16 K and to calculate the pressure p(/spl epsiv/,T) of the helium from the fundamental constants, quantum mechanics, and statistical mechanics. If the molar polarizability of helium A/sub /spl epsiv// is calculated more accurately, the proposed pressure standard might attain relative standard uncertainty of 6/spl times/10/sup -6/ for pressures near 1 MPa, a result of considerable interest to pressure metrology.

articleTitle: Cryogenic optical resonators for lasers and parametric oscillators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time frequency stabilization of an optical parametric oscillator to a reference cavity. An ultrastable cryogenic sapphire optical cavity is employed. An upper limit for its drift has been determined by comparison with an iodine hyperfine transition frequency to be <200 Hz/day.

articleTitle: Standards of distorted signal for calibration of total harmonic distortion meters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper a survey and evaluation of some progressive approaches to the standards of non-linear distortion is reported. Some types of standards of signals with known total harmonic distortion are proposed. This article is based on our previous work directed at the development of a multifunctional THD standard which is now used in the Czech Metrological Institute.

articleTitle: Characterization parameters and modelling of high frequency nonlinear devices require new calibration techniques
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The fast growing telecommunication market is suffering from the lack of good characterization and modelling tools for high frequency nonlinear devices and systems. This paper argues that accurate broadband measurements of incident and reflected waves or voltage and currents at the device ports are the essential foundation for any solution to high frequency nonlinear problems. To establish these measurement techniques in industry, there is a need for an additional calibration standard to make the measurements traceable.

articleTitle: Precision computer-controlled decade capacitor
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A precision computer-controlled decade capacitor switching capacitance values from 100 pF to 1 /spl mu/F in steps of 100 pF with an uncertainty of the order 10/sup -6/ is described. To minimize the temperature influence, special ceramic capacitors with temperature coefficients of 10/sup -6/ K/sup -1/ and low loss factor are used. Switching impedances are avoided by a four-terminal-pair definition of capacitors and quasi-coaxial connection. The capacitor can be used for automatic calibrations of capacitance bridges with a basic accuracy of 10/sup -4/ to 10/sup -5/.

articleTitle: Microwave multimeter for high level power control
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. This report is devoted to the problem of designing and constructing built-in multiprobe analyzers of microwave signals and filter parameters. The authors consider the structure of a universal passing power sensor, based on the absorbing wall principle, used for high level passing power measurements.

articleTitle: Toward compact clocks with cold cesium atoms
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present first a new 3-dimensional cooling configuration with isotropic light. We demonstrate that this cooling technique is very efficient and easy to operate. Secondly, we present two simple clock configurations using a source of atoms cooled in isotropic light. We expect these clocks to be very compact with good frequency performances.

articleTitle: Development of a mercury battery voltage standard operated at 0/spl deg/C
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This contribution describes the development of a mercury battery voltage standard operated at 0/spl deg/C. This standard was developed to examine the effect of a decrease of temperature on the stability of the standard. The first measurements indicate that the drift rate of the standard decreases with decreasing temperature.

articleTitle: Hamon transfer capacitor usable as decade capacitor
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: To extend capacitance ranges of 10 /spl mu/F to 10000 /spl mu/F, we have developed two Hamon transfer capacitors; one is 10/1000 /spl mu/F using the polycarbonate capacitor elements and the other is 100/10000 /spl mu/F using electrolytic tantalum capacitor elements. These are also able to be used as single capacitor or a decade capacitor by means of selecting the switches.

articleTitle: Comparison of dipole antenna properties calculated by assuming a sinusoidal current distribution with properties calculated using method of moments
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Two methods for calculating the properties of dipole antennas on an ideal open area test site are compared: assumption of a sinusoidal current distribution on the dipoles and the method of moments. It is shown how agreement between the methods of better than 0.07 dB can be obtained for the coupling between two dipoles over a perfectly conducting ground plane at resonance by using a very thin resonant wire in the sinusoidal current distribution calculation in place of the actual resonant wire.

articleTitle: Behavior of the Kramers-Kronig relation for measurement noise
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper the behavior of Kramers-Kronig relation is investigated. In practice measurements are used to calculate the Kramers-Kronig integral. Several integration procedures to solve this integral are discussed in the literature. However, the results of such procedures are often quite sensitive to the form of the measurement noise. It is the aim of this paper to clarify the influence of the measurement noise.

articleTitle: 1000-V-resistor for ac-dc voltage transfer
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The new design of a 1000-V-resistor on a thick AlN substrate with very high heat conductance results in minimum resistor temperature of less than 4 K above ambient. As all the Joule heat is conducted through the substrate to outside heat exchangers the inside electrostatic shield as well as the outer cylinder stay at ambient temperature. This design will result in an optimum ac-dc voltage transfer standard for the step-up from 300 V to 1000 V and frequencies from 20 kHz to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: First accuracy projection for the high C-field Cs beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The high C-field Cs beam frequency standard is presently a working machine which is undergoing first accuracy evaluations. The projected 10/sup -14/ accuracy goal is as yet unattained mainly because of inadequate C-field uniformity and stability. An analysis of the projected possible C-field improvements and the consequent uncertainty is here reported.

articleTitle: Microwave frequency sensitivity of Josephson array systems
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The hysteretic SIS Josephson array chips at the heart of current Josephson dc voltage calibration systems are known to operate more stably at some microwave frequencies than at others. We report measurements made on the microwave frequency dependence of the chip behaviour and the variation of this dependence over time.

articleTitle: Analysis and calculation of systemic error of voltage difference method in the calibration for heavy DC sensors
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A method of analyzing and calculating the systemic error of the voltage difference method in the calibration for heavy DC sensors is developed. For both current-voltage sensor and current-current sensor, the expressions for their systematic error are derived. The definitions of the methodical error are discussed. The rules for the reasonable selection of parameters of the equipment used for the calibration system are given.

articleTitle: Narrow line cooling of strontium to the recoil limit
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Experimental results on narrow line cooling of strontium atoms is presented. Cooling is performed on the /sup 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 1/ intercombination transition at 689 nm resulting in temperatures near the recoil limit in 1-D molasses.

articleTitle: Design of flux-gate magnetometer with tiny probe
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A tiny flux-gate sensor using amorphous alloy core is studied and applied to designing a magnetometer; the resolution is 1 nT and the range is up to 250 /spl mu/T for the measurement of constant low magnetic field.

articleTitle: A precision 10 mA current shunt is used to calibrate AC current at 1 mA and 100 /spl mu/A levels
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The calibration of low AC current at 1 mA and 100 /spl mu/A is described using current divider techniques. Uncertainties are calculated for 9:1 and 99:1 current division ratios. A builddown method is used stepping from 10 mA to 1 mA and from 1 mA to 100 /spl mu/A using a NIST-calibrated 10 mA current shunt as the reference.

articleTitle: Single-flux-quantum counters for advanced Josephson primary voltage standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Josephson primary voltage standards require a frequency-locked 77 GHz signal source to perform precise frequency-to-voltage conversion. We describe superconducting digital frequency counter being developed for frequency locking. Since it eliminates some system components, this counter reduces the cost of Josephson primary standards significantly.

articleTitle: Test of a space cold atom clock prototype in absence of gravity
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In space, thanks to micro-gravity conditions, a clock using laser cooled atoms is expected to have a better performance than on Earth. We have constructed a prototype of this space clock. It was tested in the absence of gravity of aircraft parabolic flights, yielding an atomic resonance with a width of 7 Hz, twice narrower than on Earth.

articleTitle: Some recent results of STFS broadcast via INSAT-possibility of accurate geostationary satellite position determination
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We describe experimental results of sub-microsecond time transfer using the one way broadcast of Standard Time and Frequency Signals (STFS) via INSAT. These are in good agreement with our earlier model computations. We also describe a technique to determine the position coordinates of the geostationary satellite INSAT-1D based on multistation recordings of the error residuals of the STFS time transfer.

articleTitle: Critical aspects of scanning X-ray/optical interferometry
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We are presently developing and testing an X-ray and optical interferometer capable of millimeter scans. Our goal is to reduce the relative uncertainty in the measurement of the (220) lattice spacing of a silicon crystal to a few parts in 10/sup 9/. In a new series of measurements, the value obtained with our previous experimental set-up is confirmed and the bounds to the measurement uncertainty are investigated.

articleTitle: Two-frequency synthesizer with shaped quantization noise [for impedance bridges]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Some impedance bridges require a signal source of accurately known frequency, and sinusoidal waveform of good spectral purity. These requirements are here met by combining the functions of synthesis and waveform generation to produce a signal that is free from phase modulation. Sidebands resulting from quantization errors are shaped to reduce those adjacent to the signal, at the expense of more remote sidebands where filtering is more effective.

articleTitle: Reestablishment of the primary AC voltage standard at KRISS
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Thin-film multijunction thermal converters have been introduced as primary AC-DC voltage transfer standards at KRISS. The evaluation of the standards from an extensive series of comparisons and analysis of the error sources by using a new automatic AC-DC difference measurement system and the fast-reversed DC source is described. The agreement between the two systems is better than 1 ppm up to 4 V and 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Magnetometer calibration set-up controlled by nuclear magnetic resonance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In order to calibrate magnetometer sensors in the field range from 2 mT to 150 mT a measuring setup consisting of a water-cooled multilayer solenoid and an NMR-magnetometer of the marginal oscillator type has been developed. With a coil constant of about 20 mT/A the field coil provides a field profile with two flat regions, where the field maxima are equal within 10/sup -5/ and with a distance of more than 40 mm so that both magnetometer readings can simultaneously be compared. The NMR-magnetometer operates with samples having an absorption line width of 2 /spl mu/T with a sample volume of 2 cm/sup 3/ for fields below 20 mT and of 1 cm/sup 3/ for higher fields.

articleTitle: Characterisation of resistance and capacitance standards up to 1 MHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. New four terminal-pair resistance and capacitance impedance standards are being fabricated for use at high frequencies ranging from 10 kHz to 1 MHz. The standards have been designed to ensure low frequency dependence of their impedance up to 1 MHz. A brief outline of the fabrication of the standards is described. A high frequency four terminal-pair impedance ratio bridge used to characterise these standards is also discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of the traveling standard for an international comparison of DC voltage ratio
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An international comparison of DC voltage ratio up to 1000 V has been started. It is one of the electrical key-comparisons selected by the CCEM. Preliminary work carried out by the pilot laboratory, IEN, in order to characterize the candidate traveling standard is reported.

articleTitle: Properties of iodine cells contaminated by the heteromolecule /sup 127/I/sup 129/I for metrological applications
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The influence of contamination of the iodine cell by heteroisotopic molecule is discussed. Numerical model results are compared with measured values for both third (THT) and fifth (FHT) harmonic method of detection. Contamination causes substantially lower frequency shift in the case of FHT.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilized 543 nm He-Ne laser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Saturated absorption signals with good S/N of the hyperfine structure of the lines R(12)26-0 and R(106)28-0 of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ in external cells were observed and used to lock the frequency of 543 nm He-Ne laser with the third harmonic technique. The two mode balance technique, by heating or cooling laser tube, was used for stabilizing the 543 nm He-Ne laser frequency. We prefer the latter.

articleTitle: A frequency standard based on a continuous beam of laser cooled atoms
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A frequency standard based on a continuous beam of laser cooled atoms as an alternative to a pulsed scheme of an atomic fountain is currently investigated. A general overview of such a device and its main parts are presented. Two mechanisms of continuous extraction of atoms from an anisotropic magneto-optical trap are experimentally demonstrated. Stability and accuracy issues are discussed.

articleTitle: A capacitance standard based on counting electrons: progress report
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have combined an electron pump and a vacuum-gap capacitor to create a prototype capacitance standard based on electron counting. We are testing various components individually to determine whether a standard with an overall uncertainty of 1 part in 10/sup 8/ is feasible.

articleTitle: Common-view technique applied to the link CENAM-LAPEM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In order to improve the quality of its time and frequency services the Mexican electricity company (Comision Federal de Electricidad, CFE) by its test on equipment and materials laboratory (Laboratorio de Pruebas y Equipos de Mexico, LAPEM), requires traceability to time and frequency Mexican primary standards. A TTR-6A GPS receiver is being employed by LAPEM in order to get this objective, and the common-view technique between CENAM-LAPEM is considered.

articleTitle: About the existing discrepancy in the determinations of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The values for the Avogadro constant, derived from the atomic and molar volume of silicon at several metrological institutes, show significant differences. To illuminate this discrepancy, comparison measurements of density, lattice parameters and positron annihilation were performed. The existing differences cannot be explained by the residual point defect contents but probably by small voids in the lattice.

articleTitle: A numerical simulation on thermoelectric effects in single-junction thermal converters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The thermoelectric effects in thermal converters have characteristic time-constants which can be evaluated from fast-reversed DC (FRDC) measurements. A numerical simulation for the FRDC measurement was performed to evaluate the relationship between the time-constants and the location of the thermoelectric effects on the length of the heater.

articleTitle: AC-DC thermal converter with IR-transmissive fiber coupling
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Single heater thermal converters and dual heater isothermal converters are realized by depositing thin-film heaters on thin dielectric membranes on a silicon chip and by remotely sensing their temperature with radiation sensors through infrared transmissive fibers. This reduces diversion of heat from the heaters as well as minimizing heater signal coupling to the sensors. The use of infrared transmissive fibers to couple the thermal energy from the heater to the radiation sensor, permits sensing the temperature directly above the heater. Distributed fibers permit collection of the radiation from the entire surface of the heater, and to design the heater for optimum frequency response.

articleTitle: Frequency stability measurements of 1.5 /spl mu/m erbium lasers locked to acetylene absorption lines
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on the absolute frequency stabilization of Yb,Er:glass laser against different acetylene absorption line in the 1.5 /spl mu/m region. Beat-note measurements between two independently stabilized lasers yield a short-term (1-ms) laser linewidth of 50 kHz and a long-term (1-hour) rms frequency fluctuation of 170 kHz. The Allan standard deviation at 0.1 s is 4/spl times/10/sup -11/.

articleTitle: A network for verifying AC resistance measuring instruments
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A resistance network for verifying the accuracy of resistance measuring instruments up described. The network has been instrument accuracies from 50 Hz to 1 MHz. Relative standard uncertainties of the method range from better than 1/spl times/10/sup -6/ at low frequency to 100/spl times/10/sup -6/ at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: A comparative study on the calibration of pole caps for a magnetic microbalance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Calibration curves for 177 mm Henry profile pole caps of a Faraday microbalance magnet are obtained from absolute susceptibility measurements. The pole caps are at gaps of 4.0, 4.5 and 5.0 cm for maximum magnetic field strengths from 2.18 to 6.90 kOe. Typical results on few standard substances are compared with reported values. An error less than 3% can be achieved for samples of limited size and sufficiently free from ferromagnetic impurities.

articleTitle: A transportable multivalue inductance standard for the range of 0,1-1000 H
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new multivalue transportable standard of the inductance unit is described which has been developed on the basis of active equivalents for the inductance range of 0.1-1000 H at a frequency from 40 Hz up to 10 kHz and an uncertainty of 0.02-0.1%.

articleTitle: Correction of systematic effects in digitizing oscilloscopes
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper presents a procedure to improve the accuracy of a digital sampling oscilloscope in the acquisition of complex waveforms. Using suitable calibration data, additive correction terms are calculated, and a criterion is given to determine when correction uncertainty is acceptable.

articleTitle: Intercomparison for RF power in 3,5 mm coaxial line up to 26 GHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The results of an international comparison of measurements of RF power in 3,5 mm coaxial line at 7 frequencies up to 26 GHz are presented. Three national laboratories of metrology with different measuring methods participated in the comparison. Good agreement between the mean values reported by the participants is observed.

articleTitle: Laser spectroscopy of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ hyperfine structure near 532 nm with diode-pumped intracavity-doubled YAG lasers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The hyperfine spectrum of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ near 532nm has been studied via modulation transfer spectroscopy using a diode-pumped intracavity-doubled ring YAG laser. Doppler-free absorption-lines in rovibrational transitions are observed. The frequency stabilization is in progress.

articleTitle: Laser-cooled Rb clocks
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. We have constructed a prototype of an /sup 87/Rb atomic fountain clock. We will report experimental results including a measurement of the cold collision shift. Calculations suggest that the shift should be 15 times smaller than that for a Cs fountain clock.

articleTitle: Charge offset and noise in SET transistors [for capacitance standard application]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on several previous and ongoing investigations into the source of, and the amelioration of, the charge offset noise in SET (single-electron tunneling) transistors, made of Al/AlO/sub x//Al tunnel junctions. Previous work has shown that significant time-dependent noise will arise from locations outside the tunnel junctions, as well as within the junctions. Our ongoing work includes attempts to reduce or eliminate the charge offset and noise in fabricated devices.

articleTitle: Fragmentation of SiF/sub 4/ in the Avogadro amount comparator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The determination of the correction factors for isotope fractionations for measurements of amount ratios of silicon-bearing ions has been undertaken in order to define correction equations for the isotope amount ratios measured on the SiF/sub 3//sup +/ ion beams used in the re-determinations of the Avogadro constant.

articleTitle: A 29 THz OsO/sub 4/ stabilized reference laser for linking the 474 THz HeNe/I/sub 2/ optical standard to the 445 THz single strontium ion standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A 29 THz, CO/sub 2/ laser system stabilized using the method of transfer modulation on a narrow transition of OsO/sub 4/ is described. By difference frequency mixing this radiation and 474 THz radiation referenced to a HeNe/I/sub 2/ laser standard, sufficient 445 THz power is obtained for heterodyne measurement against a Sr/sup +/ single ion standard.

articleTitle: Studies on frequency stabilization of Nd:YAG laser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present our studies on: (1) absolute frequency measurement of Nd:YAG laser locked to Cs/sub 2/ transitions; (2) Nd:YAG laser locked to Doppler-broadened lines of iodine; and (3) Nd:YAG laser locked to CO/sub 2/ overtone transition.

articleTitle: Bismuth germanate and lithium niobate in DC and extra-low-frequency electrooptic sensor
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Performance of bismuth germanate and lithium niobate crystals in an extra-low-frequency (ELF) and DC electrooptic sensor was investigated experimentally. Unwanted effects of conductivity, photoconductivity and stimulated conductivity of the crystals are reported. It is shown that only lithium niobate can be used as a DC field sensor.

articleTitle: A broadband microwave radiometer using correlation technique
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A broadband microwave radiometer of the differential type has been designed by adopting a correlation scheme with a quadrature hybrid coupler and its usefulness experimentally evaluated over 6 to 12.4 GHz. The correlator offers in-phase and quadrature-phase outputs. The advantage of this correlator has been investigated.

articleTitle: Results of geodetic time transfer on an European baseline
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: First results of the comparison of different atomic clocks carried out between European laboratories using a new method, called geodetic time transfer, are reported.

articleTitle: The determination of the Avogadro constant-not simply a metrological problem
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A new round in the determination of the Avogadro constant is under way at PTB and at other national metrological institutes as a step towards an alternative definition of the SI unit of mass. The required measurements of the relevant crystal data are currently hampered by an (unexpected and not yet total identified) imperfection of the crystal lattice.

articleTitle: A new determination of G
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A determination of G, the Newtonian constant of gravitation, has been made utilizing a new free-fall method. Traditionally this determination has been made using a torsion fiber which (functionally) eliminates g (the acceleration due to gravity) from the measurement process. In this determination, we explicitly use g to measure G. We do this by measuring the effect a large, yet moveable, mass has on the measured value of g. In this determination we use a FG-5 absolute gravimeter to measure g. This commercial instrument uses time-resolved interferometry of a freely falling "mirror" to determine g with a measurement accuracy approaching 1 part in 10/sup 9/. Together with the FG-5, we use a large and finely moveable mass which surrounds the dropping region. On twenty-minute intervals this mass is moved between positions just above and just below this region. As a result, the measured value of g is square-wave modulated with a peak-to-peak amplitude of approximately 80 parts in 10/sup 9/. This precisely measured difference together with a straightforward, though numerically involved, analysis of the effects of the mass in the two positions on the measured value of g determine G.

articleTitle: Silicon lattice comparisons related to the Avogadro project: uniformity of new material and surface preparation effects
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: New silicon material specifically produced for the Avogadro project has been surveyed for lattice parameter uniformity with a relative uncertainty near 1/spl times/10/sup -8/. Samples distributed longitudinally and radially have been used. Unexpected dependence of lattice parameter values on surface preparation has been noted.

articleTitle: An automated secondary standard measurement system for the characterization of soft magnetostrictive materials
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A computerized secondary standard measurement system, concerning the characterization of soft magnetostrictive materials by means of measuring their dynamic magnetoelastic behavior, has been developed and is presented.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency atlas of 9 molecular I/sub 2/ lines at 532 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Within the Nd laser tuning range, modulation transfer spectroscopy recovers nine strong ro-vibrational transitions of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ molecules with excellent signal-to-noise ratios. These transitions are now frequency-linked together, with their absolute frequencies referred to the R(56)32-0:a/sub 10/ component. Hyperfine structure splittings for the two "new" lines are fit with residuals /spl sim/500 Hz.

articleTitle: International comparison of noise-temperature measurements at 2, 4, and 12 GHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report results of a recent international comparison of thermal noise-power measurements, performed under the auspices of CIPM/CCE. The noise temperatures of two solid-state sources with GPC-7 connectors were measured at 2, 4, and 12 GHz. All results agreed within the expanded uncertainties. The comparison was performed in accordance with the guidelines recently adopted by the CCE.

articleTitle: Progress towards a precision measurement of the helion magnetic moment in Bohr magnetons
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report the progress towards a measurement of the helion magnetic moment measured in Bohr magnetons. We expect to have taken data by CPEM 98 and hope to present a preliminary result. Also described is a proposed measurement of the electron to unshielded proton magnetic moment ratio.

articleTitle: Sub-nanometric metrology for high resolution astrometric interferometry
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A study team, funded by the European Space Agency, is working on some scientific and technological aspects of a future astrometric space mission. In this framework, we are carrying out an experiment which aims at define the bounds to the performance of the metrology subsystem necessary to the sub-nanometric stabilization of stellar interferometers in space.

articleTitle: Composition and structure of surfaces of silicon spheres used in determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The Avogadro constant is required to be determined with an uncertainty of less than 1/spl times/10/sup -8/ in order to consider an atomic definition of the kilogram. A single crystal silicon sphere 93.6 mm diameter is used for this determination. Surface contaminants such as oxide and water must be taken into account. The nature of this contamination has been investigated using optical ellipsometry and ion beam analysis.

articleTitle: Non destructive evaluation sensor based on magnetostrictive delay lines
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A sensing principle is proposed in this paper concerning non-destructive evaluation of metallic surfaces. The sensing principle is based on the magnetostrictive delay line technique, allowing yokeless operation and only two orthogonal motions for a complete specimen characterization.

articleTitle: What do we actually know on the proton radius?
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We give a critical discussion on different ways to determine the proton charge radius. It is demonstrated that the best results of its measurement can be obtained from evaluation of the Mainz data on the electron-proton elastic scattering, but the uncertainty has to be large by factor two. A review of the hydrogen Lamb shift experiments and the radius determination from them is also presented.

articleTitle: Accurate frequency measurements in the infrared using stabilized CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ lasers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new calibration of an OsO/sub 4/ absolute frequency grid is reported with an uncertainty less than 100 Hz in the 28/29 THz range (/spl delta/v/v/spl sim/3/spl times/10/sup -17/). A precedent determination has been performed fifteen years before, with uncertainties ranging from 50 Hz to 2 kHz. These OsO/sub 4/ transitions confer high metrological performances to CO/sub 2/ lasers when frequency locked on the third harmonic of the saturated resonances. We report also recent results on the stability of the BNM-LPTF CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ optical frequency standard in terms of short-term stability of 3/spl times/10/sup -14//spl tau//sup - 1/2 / and long term stability of 2.4/spl times/10/sup -15/ for 3000 s of integration time. This result corresponds, to our knowledge, to the best stability achieved, up to now, in the optical domain.

articleTitle: Measurement of magnetic material properties at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new measurement method of the magnetoimpedance at high frequency is hereby proposed. The method is based on the S-parameter measurement of a specific cell consisting of a section of magnetic sample in the form of wire or ribbon suspended on a ground plane. Some experimental results are reported to show the effectiveness of the technique.

articleTitle: Smart annealing system for amorphous magnetic wires
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper presents a smart system able to control the stress-annealing process applied on the amorphous magnetic wires. The feature of these materials consists in the absence of the magneto-crystalline interaction. Therefore, the magnetic domain structure is mainly given by the magnetoelastic coupling between magnetostriction and the internal stresses. These stresses induced by controlled stress annealing allow the obtaining of materials having new magnetic properties required in special applications.

articleTitle: Developments in coaxial power standards at NPL
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A 2.4 mm twin line coaxial calorimeter is the first microwave power standard in this line size to be developed at the National Physical Laboratory. The instrument will provide traceable power measurements from dc to 50 GHz and has an effective efficiency ranging from 101.1% at 1.0 GHz to 92.2% at 50.0 GHz.

articleTitle: The measurement of modulated radiosignal parameters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The problems connected with the normalization and the measurement of modulated signal parameters are considered.

articleTitle: Parametric nonlinear supernarrow resonances in the susceptibility spectrum of a three-level atomic system in multimode strong radiation at the main transition and the weak biharmonic probe field
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. One of the leading directions of nonlinear laser spectroscopy is a study of interaction of radiation with material. The purpose of the work is to research effects of amplification of radiation without creation of initial inversion of population levels in three-level atomic media. Calculation of generation parameters in three-level systems on the main transition will allow to get a generation at frequencies where creating the usual lasers is difficult (ultraviolet and X-ray area).

articleTitle: Suggested triple-series connection measurement tests of the AC quantized Hall resistance and the AC longitudinal resistance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Based on equivalent circuit calculations a single AC ratio bridge can be used to accurately determine the AC quantized Hall resistance and to provide an independent value of the AC longitudinal resistance in a quantum Hall device. This may be achieved by making quantized Hall resistance measurements for two different combinations of triple-series connections to a standards-quality device.

articleTitle: Progress of the prompt (n,/spl gamma/)-spectrometry for the Avogadro-project
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The spectrometry of promptly emitted /spl gamma/-rays after thermal neutron capture is used for a complete, nondestructive, isotopic material analysis developed at the PTB. This method is independent of the sample dimensions and its state of aggregation. Furthermore all isotopes are detected by multi-channel analysis, simultaneously. Isotopic mass differences have been determined with an uncertainty of 10/sup -10/.

articleTitle: Waveguide-junction test cells
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The classification of the cells, based on waveguide junction, aimed at the measurement and test of magnetodielectric parameters of bars and plates has been suggested in this work. The physics of the eigen and quasi-eigen modes, that are specially located in the junctions, through which the sample under test is consecutively moved is set forth. The recommendations for choosing the optimized cell are brought forward. This choosing depends upon the purpose of measurement and test.

articleTitle: A precision DC HV voltmeter based on collinear spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Collinear laser spectroscopy is applied to translate the voltage measurement to a determination of optical frequencies, which avoids systematic errors induced by voltage dividers. The determination of the dopplershift of optical transitions gives the voltage. A prototype is to operate at 50 kV, while the project finally aims at 300 kV.

articleTitle: Towards a cheaper, simpler quantized Hall resistance standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have produced and characterised devices suitable for accurate quantum Hall resistor (QHR) measurements at fields below 8 T, and temperatures of 1.2-1.5 K. We have made accurate comparisons of QHR devices with wirewound resistors using commercially available room-temperature dc current-comparator bridges. These two results imply that it is possible to assemble an accurate, but relatively cheap and simple to operate, QHR standard.

articleTitle: A novel stabilization method for an optical frequency comb generator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Reliable operation of an optical frequency comb generator requires to lock the laser frequency to the generator. We present a novel stabilization scheme that uses the polarization state of the output light of the comb generator to derive a suitable error signal without introducing any additional modulation.

articleTitle: Thin-film cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We analyse a thin-film cryogenic current comparator (CCC) intended to be used in ac measurements. Our analysis shows that calibrating the dc ratio error of the thin-film CCC against a conventional CCC, it can be used up to 10 kHz as a sensitive and highly accurate current comparator. We have fabricated a practical 1:1 planar CCC integrated with a low-noise SQUID magnetometer.

articleTitle: Development of a high value resistor reference system at TPYCEA
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A High Value Resistor (HVR) reference system has been developed. It consists of a set of seven resistors from 100 M/spl Omega/ to 100 T/spl Omega/. The resistor set is measured with two methods: a modified Wheatstone bridge and an integration system based on the charge time of a capacitor.

articleTitle: Improvements in the quantum Hall resistance standard at VTT
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes improvements in the realisation of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) resistance standard at VTT and presents the results of the latest measurements. A new superconducting magnet and a new QHE sample were used to calibrate standard resistors in terms of R/sub K-90/, (R/sub K-90/=25812.807 /spl Omega/ is the conventional value of the von Klitzing constant R/sub K/). A 100 /spl Omega/ standard resistor was calibrated directly against the quantum Hall resistance (QHR) on i=2 plateau using a low-frequency cryogenic ac resistance bridge based on the cryogenic current comparator (CCC). The same cryogenic ac bridge was used to trace the 1 /spl Omega/ and 10 k/spl Omega/ standard resistors from the 100 /spl Omega/ standard.

articleTitle: Contactless measurements of the internal capacitance of a Corbino ring in the quantum Hall regime
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A fully inductive technique allows to observe the quantum Hall effect without any probe to the two dimensional electron gas. The ac response of the measuring system is described by a model taking into account the effect of the intrinsic capacitance of the Corbino ring.

articleTitle: Properties of Shapiro steps in pulse-driven non-hysteretic Josephson junctions
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The behavior of a non-hysteretic shunted Josephson junction can be described by a differential equation admitting analytical solution in the constant current bias case. Studying the pulse bias as a sequence of constant bias states we were able to derive expressions for the phase lock condition and study some relevant features of Shapiro steps.

articleTitle: Measurement of the muonium 1S-2S transition frequency
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new measurement of the 1S-2S energy splitting of muonium by Doppler-free two-photon spectroscopy has been performed at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory in Chilton, Didcot, UK. Increased accuracy is expected compared to a previous experiment. Spectroscopy of this transition promises an improvement of the muon mass value.

articleTitle: Frequency doubling of a diode laser near 633 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report on efficient frequency doubling of a diode laser near 633 nm using a rubidium dihydrogen phosphate crystal in a resonant cavity, with 30 /spl mu/W of output power. Stabilization of the pump laser to the Doppler-free spectrum of iodine at 633 nm provides a possibility for a stable frequency standard at 317 nm.

articleTitle: A guarded transfer standard for high resistance measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An improved design for a guarded transfer standard in the resistance range 1 M/spl Omega/ to 100 G/spl Omega/ is described. Existing transfer standards and limitations are reviewed. Interchangeable guard networks are used in the improved transfer standards to ensure complete guarding during all phases of the measurement process thus reducing errors caused by leakages to ground.
