articleTitle: Quantum manipulation and measurement of single atoms in optical cavity QED
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given. Using cold atoms strongly interacting with individual photons inside a high finesse cavity, we are approaching an ideal quantum system in which both matter (internal and external degrees of freedom) and light exhibit strong quantum character and the system's coherent evolution dominates decoherence processes. With this system we have performed real-time continuous measurement of single atomic spatial trajectories. The measurement protocol involves the determination of the phase of the cavity output field, which is far-detuned from the atomic resonance to minimize the measurement back action on the center-of-mass (CM) motion. The real-time evolution of the complex field amplitude is efficiently recorded at high bandwidth and with good signal-to-noise ratio, limited respectively by the rate of coherent coupling between atom and cavity mode and the photodetection shot noise. This nearly optimal detection technique has already revealed atomic CM motion inside the cavity standing-wave field of single photons, and should eventually lead to the strong conditioning of system evolution on measurement results and the realization of quantum feedback control. Another related but independent experiment concentrates on quantum manipulation of the CM motion. Owing to the highest coherent coupling rate between cavity field and individual atoms achieved to date, the mechanical coupling between atom and cavity can be significantly larger than the kinetic energy of laser cooled atoms, even under very low cavity excitation. Indeed, evidence of mechanical light forces for intracavity photon number <1 has already been observed. The origin of this mechanical force is radically different from that in conventional laser trapping where photon scattering (coherent or incoherent) drives the atomic CM motion. The spatial variation of the standing cavity mode (and hence of the atom-field coupling), produce optical potentials capable of localizing atoms inside the cavity. With the initial evidence of prolonged atomic transit through the cavity field (by 3/spl times/) when the suitable trapping state (the lower dressed state of the atom-cavity system) was excited, we are working towards suppression of the atomic momentum diffusion to achieve long-term atomic confinement via quantum feedback.

articleTitle: Measurements of torsion fiber anelastic properties in preparation for a new measurement of G
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present results of measurements of anelastic properties of CuBe and Al5056 torsion fibers at low temperature, and discuss their implications for a planned measurement of G using a cryogenic torsion pendulum. It appears that anelastic behavior should not limit a G measurement at a level of a few ppm.

articleTitle: Effect of temporary temperature change on drift rate of KRISS legal ohm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The abnormal drift rate of Thomas type 1 ohm resistors according to temporary temperature change is described and they are compared with NML 1 ohm resistors with almost the same drift rate. It is thought that the major origin of difference between the two types is the coil-mounting structure suffering from stress.

articleTitle: A highly linear frequency ramp generator based on a fractional divider phase-locked-loop
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A synthesizer based on a fractional divider concept for generating highly linear analog frequency ramps is presented. Numerical simulations promise a very good precision of such a ramp generator which has been proved by implementing a prototype synthesizer circuit in a FMCW-radar system. The simulations as well as the measurements obtained with the prototype circuit are shown.

articleTitle: A new design of precision inductance bridge
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In high precision measurement of inductance the residuals resulting from the great number of resistance and capacitance elements in the variable arm of the Owen bridge can introduce significant errors. In order to minimize these errors the present paper describes a new design of all the bridge decades in which a minimum number of elements is used.

articleTitle: Progress towards an optical frequency chain at NPL
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An optical frequency chain is being constructed at NPL with the object of making absolute frequency measurements of optical frequency standards in single, cold, trapped Sr/sup +/ and Yb/sup +/ ions. The initial frequency reference will be a methane-stabilized He-Ne laser system but our ultimate goal is an all-optical chain to the caesium primary microwave frequency standard.

articleTitle: Medium size cryogenic current comparator as very low current amplifier
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes the realisation of a medium size CCC (30000:1 windings ratio) and the experimental optimisation of its sensitivity. First results reported on give a sensitivity of 7.7 /spl mu/A. turn per flux quantum.

articleTitle: A Bayesian expression for the recalibrated value
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Taking into account the result of previous calibration in the recalibration of a measurement device is considered in frame of the Bayesian approach. An expression for the recalibrated value is obtained for the case when the recalibration is performed by measuring the quantity which value is known prior to the measurement from other sources. The possible correlation between the value obtained in the previous calibration and the value measured in course of the recalibration is taken into the consideration. The expressions obtained can also be applied for calculation of the results of some comparisons of the standards.

articleTitle: A new 60 GHz open resonator method for precision permittivity and loss tangent measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new method is developed for the determination of loss tangent and dielectric permittivity of ultra low absorbing materials at 60 GHz. The micrometer and the stepping motor driven flat mirror in the Fabry-Perot cavity can now be scanned at a very small steps (to change the cavity length or mirror spacing) to provide a complete interferogram over the entire Gaussian profile. The length of the cavity can now be varied at a step size as small as 20 nanometers. It is no longer necessary to use explicit formulae in the determination of the loss tangent and permittivity parameters in this way.

articleTitle: An isolated 1 V Josephson voltage reference
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We operate a 1 V Josephson Junction array continuously in a low-loss storage dewar with only a small increase in the rate of helium loss. Microwave power at 86 GHz is applied to the array via an unclad dielectric waveguide and is switched by moving an absorber close to the guide. The operation of the array is fully automated and the array is biased and its voltage determined by an isolated bias source and voltmeter, either of which can be disconnected after the array voltage has been set.

articleTitle: Construction of Cs atomic fountain frequency standard at NRLM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Towards the primary frequency standard with the accuracy of 10/sup -16/ level, we are developing a Cs atomic fountain at NRLM. The Cs atoms are trapped in a magneto-optical trap (MOT), cooled in the optical molasses and then launched upward. Among the six beams comprising the MOT, two beams are in the horizontal plane and other beams are oriented 45° to the vertical axis. This geometry enables multi-pulse operation, which is useful to reduce the frequency shifts due to cold collisions and the down conversion of the local oscillator noise. Recent progress in the development this frequency standard is reported.

articleTitle: An improved, optically-pumped, primary frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An improved primary frequency standard based on an optically-pumped, thermal, atomic-beam has been jointly developed by CRL and NIST. The design details along with the first evaluation and comparison with NIST's existing standard are presented.

articleTitle: Towards a programmable HTS Josephson voltage standard: recent results
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper summarized recent results of our work towards developing a voltage standard based on high-temperature (HTS) Josephson junctions array. The concept of a programmable HTS voltage standard and technological aspects of fabrication are discussed. New circuits providing uniform microwave current distribution along the HTS array are suggested.

articleTitle: The measure challenge of the LHC project
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is CERN's next accelerator project, to be commissioned in 2005. The project presents unprecedented challenges in the accurate control of high currents up to 13 kA. Around 1600 superconducting magnet circuits are deployed in the underground, 27 km circumference, tunnel. A new concept with quasi-on-line calibration is proposed.

articleTitle: Deployment of a compact, transportable, fully automated Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The development of a compact portable 10 V Josephson voltage standard has been described previously. Here we discuss modifications, accuracy intercomparisons, field testing and operator training carried out prior to its deployment as a traveling primary standard for nine NASA standards laboratories.

articleTitle: Quantifying demonstrated equivalence
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Recent debates about measurement equivalence would have been simplified by a satisfactory quantification of equivalence. We describe a rigorous yet simple method of using measurement comparisons to quantify equivalence statements. It is able to treat all aspects of the ISO Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement as they apply to measurement comparisons. We compare this method to the common usage of the normalized error.

articleTitle: A tunable iodine stabilized He-Ne laser at wavelengths 543 nm, 605 nm and 612 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A tunable iodine stabilized He-Ne laser has been constructed. The laser radiation has only one polarization state which removes the polarization flipping problem. The single mode output power of the laser is higher than 250 /spl mu/M at 543 nm. The frequency of the laser has been stabilized on the hyperfine absorption components of iodine molecular transitions R(12) 26-0, R(106) 28-0 at 543 nm, P(62) 11-2 at 605 nm and R(47) 9-2, P(48) 11-3 at 612 nm.

articleTitle: Time and frequency measurement at UME
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: UME Time and Frequency Laboratory has been member of BIPM TAI Club since 1994. UME time and frequency standard system was established using three HP 5071A Cs atomic clocks and two GPS receivers (TTR 6A and TTR 6). The accuracy and long time stability of our clocks were found to be better than 2/spl times/10/sup -13/. The time information was disseminated via telephone lines using time code generator, personal computer and modem with an accuracy of a few milliseconds.

articleTitle: Level dependence of AC-DC transfer devices
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new method is described which makes it possible to compare thermal voltage converters with a ratio of 2:1 without introducing any error due to level dependence. Measurement results are presented and error sources are analysed.

articleTitle: The strontium single ion optical frequency standard: preliminary absolute frequency measurements using a phase-locked optical frequency chain
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Absolute frequency measurements of the /sup 88/Sr/sup +/ single trapped ion 5s/sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-4d/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ reference transition at 445 THz were performed including a preliminary phase-coherent measurement linking the single ion transition to a Cs standard. An observed transition resolution below 250 Hz (FWHM) was obtained.

articleTitle: Evaluation of 100 ampere, 100 kHz transconductance amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper presents experimental evaluation of the performance of more than ten production units of a 100 A, 100 kHz transconductance amplifier. In addition to the stability, uncertainty, distortion and frequency response, these results indicate that the output impedance may be closely modeled by a parallel combination of a resistor and a capacitor. This model then proves to be very useful for correcting the errors introduced into the high-frequency high current measurements by the parasitic load inductance.

articleTitle: An advanced technique for the multipole imaging of a magnetic source: discrete transforms in high-precision magnetic signature processing
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An extension of a magnetic moment theorem for all multipoles, presented here for the first time, leads to development of an orthonormal set of discrete selective functions, applied to an accurate multipole imaging of an object by analysis of its magnetic signature (MS). The computed solution generates this orthonormal set for different trace grids. An example set is tested numerically with a non-uniform normalised grid and its selective efficiency is proved.

articleTitle: Towards an accurate frequency standard at 1.5 /spl mu/m based on the acetylene overtone band transition
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We are making a frequency standard operating at 1.5 /spl mu/m region using the saturated absorption of the /spl nu//sub 1/+/spl nu//sub 3/ band of /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ with a Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity cell. In order to obtain longer life time of the cell, we newly designed a scheme consisting of an enhancement cavity with a ULE spacer and a baked and sealed-off cell with Brewster windows. We could observe the spectrum with the linewidth of 1 MHz 10 months after since we made the cell. Two sets of the standard are made and a preliminary measurement gave the square root of the Allan variance /spl sigma/(/spl tau/)=2/spl times/10/sup -12/ at the integrating time /spl tau/=100 s.

articleTitle: New generation of electrical resistance standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Investigations of new generation resistance standards with the heightened stability to changes of air pressure, which intended for use as a traveling 100 Ohm resistance standard during international comparison of QHR. The measurements were performed in the range from 800 to 1050 mbar using a temperature regulated pressure cell.

articleTitle: Observation of "whispering gallery" modes in dielectric rod resonators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We show some preliminary observations of "whispering gallery" modes in a sapphire rod 100 mm long and 20 mm in diameter. Traditionally dielectric ring resonators or short squat resonators (D/L/spl ges/1) have been used for the observation of such modes. Results of an oscillator employing these whispering gallery modes will also be given in this paper.

articleTitle: Realisation of Croatian electromagnetic prototype of the kilogram
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The possibilities of adaptation of the existing device known as the Voltage Balance ETF-84 are considered to enable an electrostatic operation with a voltage of 100 kV and a weight of 1 kg. The balance itself and some its parts have to be reconstructed, as well as the high voltage resistor specially designed for this purpose.

articleTitle: Iodine stabilised diode laser at 633 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A diode laser has been frequency stabilised to I/sub 2/-Doppler free absorption signals. Relative frequency stability of 5.10/sup -12/ is reached at an integration time of 100 s. This compact setup provides good possibilities of implementing a portable frequency standard.

articleTitle: A laser-diode spectrometer for the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition of single laser-cooled trapped Yb/sup +/
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: For spectroscopy of the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition of Yb/sup +/, we are developing a laser-diode spectrometer composed of a master laser locked to a high-finesse cavity, a phase-locked offset laser for frequency scanning, and a frequency doubler. We detected the 6S-8S two-photon absorption of Cs to improve a long-term stability of the spectrometer.

articleTitle: Self calibrating phase standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A phase standard, consisting of clock coupled phase generator and phase meter, is proposed. Phase generator is build around two direct digital synthesizers. Phase meter incorporates a single a/d converter and a floating point. A novel approach uses a/d converter in successive sampling of two signals and compensating for an introduced phase shift by taking into account a time interval between two sampling bursts.

articleTitle: Measurement of the AC quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The flatness and frequency dependence of the i=2 and 4 quantized Hall resistance plateaux have been investigated. It was observed that for frequencies up to 6.4 kHz, a flat region exists at the centre of the plateaux where the resistance is constant to 2/spl times/10/sup -8/, and its value has a linear frequency dependence of 0.1 ppm/kHz.

articleTitle: Power standard based on a high precision power-factor meter
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A high-precision power-factor meter, based on zero crossing detectors, is proposed. The influence of the distortion in the input signals is analyzed and low pass filters proposed to prevent this error source. This system is proposed as a new power standard meter, based on the measurement of voltage, current and power factor.

articleTitle: A single channel three phase power transfer standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper deals with a three-phase a.c. thermal power comparator and a reference power converter for calibration of three-phase wattmeters and watt-hour meters, based on the above comparator. The comparator developed at the D.I. Mendeleyev Institute for Metrology (VNIIM), contains only one measurement channel in which a known d.c. power is compared to a three phase power to be measured. An a.c./d.c error of the comparator with any factor PF and asymmetrical three-phase voltage and current system does not exceed 100 ppm.

articleTitle: A multi-frequency quadrature bridge
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A quadrature bridge has been developed with the aim of determining capacitance values at several frequencies in terms of a resistance ultimately derived from the QHR. The bridge is evaluated by comparing a 1 nF capacitor with a 100 k/spl Omega/ resistor at six frequencies from 3/8/spl times/10/2/spl pi/ kHz to 10/2/spl pi/ kHz.

articleTitle: Using 10 V Josephson voltage standards to estimate the uncertainty of Zener voltage references as travelling standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In anticipation of the start of a European comparison of 10 V Josephson array voltage standards (EUROMET project 429 led by NMi VSL), the BIPM and the BNM-LCIE Josephson standards have been compared by means of Zener travelling references. An overall spread of 5 parts in 10/sup 9/ has been found with a standard uncertainty of 6 parts in 10/sup 9/. These results show that the performance of the Zener references could be the main cause of uncertainty in such a comparison.

articleTitle: Monolithic cw optical parametric oscillators for optical frequency measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In order to use as a light source for optical frequency measurement, we developed a doubly resonant, monolithic cw optical parametric oscillator, which is characterized by a low threshold and a capability of stable long term operation.

articleTitle: High-precision method for gauge block measurements and comparison of gauge block interferometers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A precise method, intended for nanometer accuracy in gauge block length measurements, has been realized. Results of the measurements are corrected on distortions in interferometer optics and are not affected by the quality of wringing and deformation of the reference plate. Accuracy limitations of the conventional method are outlined.

articleTitle: Dependence of contact resistance on current for good and bad ohmic contacts to quantized Hall resistors
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Dependence of contact resistance on current has been measured for a large number of ohmic contacts to quantized Hall resistors under quantum Hall effect conditions. A definite trend is observed in the current dependences of resistances of good and bad contacts, regardless of the physical cause of the poor contact.

articleTitle: Design and realisation of an optimal current sensitive CCC
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have designed and constructed a dedicated cryogenic current comparator (CCC) for the measurement of very small currents. The essential element of the system is a home-made SQUID with input inductance equal to that of the CCC overlapping shield (which we use as pick-up coil).

articleTitle: A precise microwave spectroscopy measurement of the muonium ground state: hyperfine structure interval and muon magnetic moment
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Data-taking has been completed on a new high precision experiment at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility (LAMPF) to determine the muonium (/spl mu//sup +/e/sup -/) ground state hyperfine structure interval /spl Delta//spl nu/ (to /spl sim/10 ppb) and the muon to proton magnetic moment ratio /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/ (to /spl sim/90 ppb), each corresponding to about a fourfold improvement compared to present knowledge.

articleTitle: A traceable mains-frequency power standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A mains-frequency power standard traceable to voltage and impedance standards has been realised. Standard uncertainties are 26 /spl mu/W/W at unity power factor, and 18 /spl mu/W/W of apparent power at zero power factor. A power bridge balanced to 0.2% is augmented by FFT analysis of samples of the detector voltage, eliminating harmonics and drift in the test sources.

articleTitle: A fuzzy-based filter for data processing of JAVS measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new approach for data processing of Josephson array voltage standard measurement results by fuzzy-based reasoning at NMC/PSB is described. It makes data processing more accurate, reliable and at least 10 times faster than processing data manually.

articleTitle: Velocity distributions and second-order Doppler shifts in an optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The velocity distribution of cesium atoms in an optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard constructed at the KRISS is obtained by using the Fourier transform of Ramsey lineshape. The velocity distribution fits well with a 1//spl upsi//sup 2/-weighted Maxwellian rather than a 1//spl upsi/-weighted one in our case. The second-order Doppler shift is -2.7/spl times/10/sup -13/.

articleTitle: Development of a frequency-doubled blue diode laser spectrometer for a calcium optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A frequency-doubled diode laser spectrometer in the blue spectral range has been developed based on a cavity-enhanced SHG method. The SHG output at 422 nm was applied for probing of a Ca atomic beam to investigate the modified velocity distribution when the beam was decelerated with a stilben-420 dye laser.

articleTitle: A metrological scanning probe microscope
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A metrological scanning probe microscope (SPM) has been jointly developed and manufactured by NIM (China) and PTB (Germany). This instrument is a "sample scan" SPM. A new and high precision scanning X-Y table (monolithic flecxible hinge type) equipped with capacitance transducers for all 6 axis and is controlled by a corresponding digital signal, and it is made of aluminum. The Z-scanner uses a built-in capacitance transducer for its active element. The X-Y scan is generated in a closed feedback-loop. This SPM includes a two tip holder in the Z-scanner, one is for tunnel-tip and the other is for needle sensor. This construction is very convenience for different types of measurement STM and AFM. The measurements of the instrument are controlled by a computer with a DSP card and a IEEE card. The IEEE card can drive the X-Y scanning table by a digital signal. The software of this system was written in C language and IDL language. The program for controling the DSP card and data collection was written in C language.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Josephson voltage standards of the Centro Espanol de Metrologia and the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Comparisons of the 1 V Josephson array voltage standard of the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures were made with that of the Centro Espanol de Metrologia, Madrid, Spain in October 1997. The results agree within an overall uncertainty of less than 1 nV.

articleTitle: Independent units: transformations and modifications of SI
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The two new classes of units of SI (Le Systeme International d'Unites), independent and dependent units, are proposed to be introduced. An analysis of the role of the independent units in transformations and modifications of SI is given. Some transformations and modifications of SI are considered.

articleTitle: Measurement intercomparisons of dielectric and magnetic material characterization
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We discuss the results of three NIST-organized intercomparisons of dielectric and magnetic material characterization at RF-microwave frequencies. Two studies used the broadband coaxial air line technique and the third the air-filled stripline resonator. Variability of up to /spl plusmn/25% was evident in the measured data.

articleTitle: Assessment of the accuracy of a vector voltmeter using a network analyser with airline and attenuation standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The phase and magnitude measurement information given by a vector voltmeter was investigated by comparison with airline and attenuation standards. Considerable errors were found and a method to reduce errors caused by the vector voltmeter using a line fitting technique was applied. The results obtained are discussed.

articleTitle: BIPM activities related to realization of the definition of the metre
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The results are presented of frequency comparisons of laser radiations at /spl lambda//spl ap/3.39 /spl mu/m, /spl lambda//spl ap/633 nm, and /spl lambda//spl ap/515 nm used for the realization of the metre. Work on lasers at /spl lambda/=532 nm, recently recommended by the CIPM, and on iodine-stabilized extended-cavity diode laser at 633 nm are described. Activities in gravimetry and in nanometrology are also presented.

articleTitle: Cryogenic current comparator measurements at 77 K using thallium-2223 thick-film shields
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes resistance ratio measurements using cryogenic current comparator (CCC) devices that operate at 77 K. The magnetic shields are Thallium-based thick films on MgO substrates. The effectiveness of three shield geometries is determined using one-to-one and ten-to-one winding ratios.

articleTitle: Requirements for an electromechanical system of superconducting magnetic levitation and means for its designing properly
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: For simulating axially symmetric systems of superconducting magnetic levitation the work suggests the program facilities for easy applying such means as varying the shape of the floating body superconducting shell, varying space distribution of the turn density of levitating coils, incorporating loops of persistent currents or superconducting sheaths over the levitating coils. The effect of applying the means to the NRLM preliminary system is demonstrated.

articleTitle: New method of digital fringe signal processing in an absolute gravimeter
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We describe a digital fringe signal processing method realized in the new Tsubokawa-type transportable absolute gravimeter. A data processing algorithm based on the second-differences method has used neither the fringes counting nor the nonlinear least squares fitting. The relative combined standard uncertainty is less than 1/spl middot/10/sup -9/ of an absolute gravity value.

articleTitle: The next generation of the NIST watt balance
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Reduction in the total uncertainty of the NIST watt balance is limited by the present configuration of the experiment. Most of the major uncertainty components arise from the fact that the experiment is performed in air. To reduce the contribution of these components, a vacuum system for the NIST watt balance has been constructed. The vacuum system and other future modifications to the NIST watt balance are discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison of two Josephson array voltage standard systems using a set of Zener references
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Two Josephson Array Voltage Standard Systems using different calibration algorithms are operated at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). A manual switch system is designed to make system comparisons by measuring against the 1.018 V of three Zener references. The difference of the average of the three Zener references is smaller than 1 nV.

articleTitle: One hundred years of metrology at the Spanish TPYCEA
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: One hundred years ago the Precision Workshop and Artillery Electrotechnical Center (TPYCEA) was created. This paper illustrates the present situation at TPYCEA, showing the standards available in three areas related with the scope of CPEM conference: dimensional interferometry, low frequency electricity and high frequency electricity.

articleTitle: Automation of a calibration laboratory [and application to thermometer calibration]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In the paper particular requirements for the automation of a typical calibration laboratory are presented. Emphasis is on laboratories performing high level calibrations, where the final stage of a calibration process is an issue of a calibration certificate. A temperature calibration laboratory based on transfer reference standards and performing calibrations by comparison is discussed.

articleTitle: A new atomic frequency standard: the coherent population trapping Cs maser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Recent studies have shown the feasibility of a Cs maser without population inversion based on the coherent population trapping phenomenon. Among the main advantages of this type of frequency standard are size, simplicity of implementation, virtual absence of first order light shift and the availability of a low noise microwave signal leading to the realization of a standard with an excellent short term frequency stability.

articleTitle: Improvement of the DC-voltage accuracy in production-line
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In order to reflect the accuracy of the production-line, the precise, but noisy DC voltage output of the PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) type calibrator is successfully measured by the Josephson instrument combined with a newly developed filter.

articleTitle: A fast switching system for AC-DC transfer measurements
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A fast (around 1 ms) switching system has been built for AC-DC transfer measurements. It comprises a control/interface unit and a separate housing for the relays. Depending on the relay unit used, the switching system can be used up to 1000 V or up to 100 MHz, and sense the applied voltages.

articleTitle: Nonperturbing electric field sensor for near field measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present a novel electric field measurement system utilising optical technology, which has been developed, tested and calibrated for near field measurement in the frequency region up to 1.8 GHz. The measuring probe is passive, all-dielectric and EMI immune. The achieved measurement resolution and minimum measurable field were 10 V/m, with a spatial resolution of 10 mm.

articleTitle: A microwave exciter system based on a sapphire loaded cavity oscillator
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A low noise and highly stable microwave exciter system has been built for Cs atomic frequency standards using a sapphire loaded cavity oscillator which works at room temperature. The construction and performance are presented.

articleTitle: A high accurate test standard of ADC, DAC and its experiment results
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An automatic test standard of the static properties of ADC and DAC and its constituted technology are introduced. With some special techniques, we made a 24 bits inside standard DAC. The test speed can be from 40 Hz/spl sim/25 kHz. The measurement results are also submitted.

articleTitle: Possible errors in inferring from sampled data the spectrum of a physical quantity's fluctuations
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: It is shown that sampled measurements of a physical quantity can produce spectral aliasing and partially mask the real spectrum of its fluctuations with excess noise. The latter appears as a white process in both spectral and variance analysis. It is argued that, conversely, no easy conclusion on the real statistical properties of a quantity's fluctuations can be made based on sampled measurements.

articleTitle: Some results and an estimate of the current uncertainty of PTB's reconstructed primary clock CS1
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper describes briefly the reconstructed primary clock CS1 of PTB and some results obtained during a one-year test period and the following quasi-routine operation. An estimate of the uncertainty is given.

articleTitle: A maximum step voltage test of 1 V Josephson junction arrays
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A maximum step voltage test of two 1-V Josepshon junction arrays fabricated at different places were performed. Maximum zero-crossing voltages, frequency of the millimeter waves, and their power are measured. These items are demonstrated to be useful to discuss performance of arrays.

articleTitle: An approach to DC voltage references long term history and quality evaluation
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Measurement data acquired on DC voltage group standards are analyzed in a new way, which allows to qualify better the individual group members long term behavior and enhance it's predictability.

articleTitle: ECG reference data set-a novel measurement standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A reference standard for testing interpreting electrocardiographs and their underlying algorithms has been developed. It consists of ECG signals of superior quality and comprehensive additional information stored in a relational data base which is accessible via the Internet.

articleTitle: Equivalence of calibration certificates between EUROMET and NIST
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The present status of a database based on comparison projects performed under EUROMET, as well as results for comparisons between NIST and EUROMET members, will be presented. The database is the result of a project to establish and validate a framework within which calibration certificates from NMIs in EU and NIST could be regarded as mutually equivalent. This equivalence would be accepted by regulatory bodies in the EU and USA for purposes of traceability requirements in regulation trade etc. based on comparisons between NMI's.

articleTitle: A digital control system for iodine stabilized lasers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A digital system for the control of iodine stabilized He-Ne lasers used as an optical frequency standard has been developed. The system is more flexible than previously developed systems and automation is incorporated. A new locking method for higher harmonic locking has been developed and included in the system. We call it the third harmonic derivative (3hD) method.

articleTitle: A basic consideration of precision electrical measurement
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The "voltage measurement circuit" and "current measurement circuit" are essential components of any precision electrical measurement system. The paper is intended to provide an introduction to proper shielding connection for the two basic circuits including N-terminals concept of measurement instrument and the generalized coaxial structure.

articleTitle: Cryo-cooled sapphire oscillator with ultra-high stability
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We present design details and test results for the first short-term frequency standard to achieve ultra-high stability (/spl sigma//sub y/<10/sup -14/) without the use of liquid helium. Technical features include vibration isolation by atmospheric helium gas and a new sapphire resonator design with adjustable compensation operating at 8-10 K.

articleTitle: Near infra-red wavelength metrology with semiconductor diode lasers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A laser spectral measurement facility has been developed in response to needs for the accurate determination of laser wavelength in the near infrared spectral region in a diversity of applications (fundamental constant determination, optical DWDM communication, environmental spectroscopy, ...). The facility is based on a number of frequency-stabilised grating cavity lasers, atomic and molecular reference cells and optical interferometers.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of a 10 pF standard capacitor between NPL and PTB
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: An intercomparison of standard capacitor of value 10 pF has been carried out between NPL (India) and Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (Germany) under the PTB-NPL Cooperation programme. The measurements of a 10 pF silica capacitor at the frequency 1592 Hz for two different temperatures agreed within 0.15 ppm.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of a Nd:YAG laser to Doppler-broadened lines of iodine near 532 nm
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Diode-pumped Nd:YAG lasers are promising sources of the new optical frequency standards at 532 nm that were recommended recently in the 9th CCDM. Molecular iodine has several strong absorption lines at the second harmonic of Nd:YAG laser near 532 nm, thus providing an absolute reference for frequency stabilization. In general, the 532 nm laser sources used in iodine-stabilized systems are commercial monolithic lasers, which are compact, efficient, and reliable, but are also expensive and complicated. Recently, we have frequency stabilized a self-developed single-frequency Nd:YAG-KTP laser to the Doppler-broadened (instead of Doppler-free) lines of iodine. That was the first time to stabilize a 532 nm laser to an absolute reference in China. Due to its concise structure, low cost, and the ability to resist more disturbance, the laser system is attractive in some certain industrial applications that require an absolute frequency reference but not very high stability.

articleTitle: A data processing method for measurement with time-drift factors and its application in AC/DC transfer standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In repeated measurements, some time-drift factors result in measurement error. In this paper, a data processing method to reduce measurement error due to such kind of time-drift factors is introduced. The efficiency of its application, especially in measurement of AC/DC transfer standard, has been described.

articleTitle: International recognition of national measurement standards and calibration certificates
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The international recognition of national measurement standards and calibration certificates issued by different National Metrology Institutes can be tested by inter-laboratory comparisons backed by a defined statistical model. However, such comparisons cannot rigorously prove equivalence and must, therefore, be supplemented by additional methods of establishing mutual confidence.

articleTitle: Automatic locking of a semiconductor laser at /spl lambda//spl ap/633 nm on linear absorption iodine transitions
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A 633 nm laser diode was frequency tuned by its injection current and was automatically locked on specific linear absorption lines of iodine by using a digital line identification system. The setup provides a low cost optical frequency reference that is precise enough to replace He-Ne references in many metrological applications.

articleTitle: Measurement of the frequency shift induced by thermal radiation in a Cs atomic fountain frequency standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have used an atomic fountain frequency standard to measure the frequency shift induced by a static electric field and a thermal field. These measurements will allow a better evaluation of the frequency shift induced by the blackbody radiation in cesium frequency standards.

articleTitle: High frequency one dimensional single electron transport in GaAs heterostructures
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Work on surface acoustic wave (SAW) induced single electron flow is described. A current given by ef is obtained where e is the electron charge and f is the frequency, near 2.8 GHz. Present accuracy for measurement of e is better than 0.1%. Prospects for improvement will be discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement system for the voltage dependence of high voltage AC-DC thermal converters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A new system for the measurement of the voltage dependence of range resistors for high voltage AC-DC thermal converters, which uses high voltage capacitors as reference, has been set up. Preliminary results of the comparison between range resistors and commercial capacitors are reported and the design of specific high voltage capacitors is described.

articleTitle: Industry benefits as a result of time dissemination at CENAM
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. With the aim of disseminating the Coordinated Universal Time Scale UTC (CENAM) and with the purpose that industry gets benefit from the time scale, we were helpers (design, coordination, test and installation) of a synchronization system which can be used in factories to synchronize clocks, computers and netservers. This system was tested in a food factory. In this application, the system included four digital clocks, a computer interface and software for updating a computer (main computer which updates these clocks). The company obtained benefits from this work as follows: 1. Improved quality in its thermal production process. 2. Reduced losses both in time and production. 3. Improved coordination among departments. We also provide time to a large TV station. A banking institution receives time within an agreement between CENAM and this institution to assist it in network synchronization.

articleTitle: The IMGC calibration set-up for microdisplacement actuators
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In the calibration of piezo-capacitive displacement actuators, use is made of an interferometric set-up with sub-nanometric resolution. In order to minimise the periodic non-linearity effect of the interferometer, accurate /spl lambda/-steps are obtained from a computer-based loop control of the out-of-phase between the reference and the measuring signal of the interferometer. Experimental results show a standard uncertainty of about 1 nm+0.7/spl middot/10/sup -4/ L//spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Automated comparator for AC-DC difference accurate measurements used at the BNM-LCIE
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes the new automated comparator used at the BNM-LCIE for the calibration of voltage thermal converters with the best level of uncertainty. It allows to achieve A-type uncertainties of the order of a few parts in 10/sup 7/ in the frequency range from 10 Hz to 1 MHz (100 kHz for voltages above 100 V). B-type measurement uncertainty depends on the type of converters to be compared and on the applied voltage level, but generally is between a few parts in 10/sup 7/ and a few parts in 10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: Response of Hall probes in the ultra-acoustic frequency range
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A setup for measurement of frequency response of Hall probes in the ultra-acoustic range is described. Field is probed inside a coaxial circuit with circular and axial symmetry, minimizing variations of field distribution with frequency and offering calculable geometry. Probe signal, and current signal from a high-frequency shunt, are acquired both with a lock-in amplifier and an ac voltmeter.

articleTitle: Precision holographic measurements of 64- meter reflector antenna in Medvezhy Ozera
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The report presents results of measurements of mirror surface on one of largest Russian radiotelescopes-64-meter antenna in a space communication centre near Moscow. Radioholographic measurements with satellites signals were fulfilled on this antenna. Restored map of main mirror shows deviations near of 2 mm rms. Rms difference of the maps measured under identical conditions was about 0.1 mm. After partial adjustment of mirror surface an antenna efficiency was increased from 0.51 to 0.65 at 5-cm band. A stability of mirror form was investigated by means of comparison of maps measured under different external conditions.

articleTitle: High-performance trapped Hg/sup +/ frequency standards
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We have demonstrated a new frequency standard, accurate to 3.4/spl times/10/sup -15/, based on the 40.5 GHz ground state hyperfine transition in cooled and trapped /sup 199/Hg/sup +/. We are also developing an optical frequency standard based on /sup 199/Hg/sup +/. The spectral width of the 563 nm laser used in this standard is less than 6 Hz.

articleTitle: Interferometric frequency measurements of an iodine stabilised Nd:YAG laser
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report the interferometric frequency measurement of frequency doubled 532 nm Nd:YAG lasers stabilised to hyperfine components in the two transitions, P(54)32-0 and R(57)32-0 of /sup 127/I/sub 2/. Two independent systems were developed using commercially available devices. Frequency stabilities of 1/spl times/10/sup -12/ for an averaging time of 1 s were achieved.

articleTitle: FET thermal converters
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Field Effect Transistor Thermal Converters (FET-TCs) use FETs working as dynamically controlled impedances, enabling an exact control of the dissipated power proportional to the product of the FET's drain voltage and source current. The temperature increase caused is directly proportional to the time-averaged internally dissipated power. A FET-TC based on MOSFETs was analysed from the thermal and electrical point of view and constructed to measure rms values of electrical ac quantities including power with uncertainties in the ppm level.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of extended cavity diode lasers to iodine at 633 nm. Review of different methods
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: In this paper we discuss different approaches to frequency stabilize extended cavity diode lasers to I/sub 2/-Doppler-free absorption signals. This includes the use of intra-cavity/extra-cavity absorption cells, and application of either third harmonic detection techniques or frequency-modulation spectroscopy.

articleTitle: New measurement capabilities of the NRC travelling standard program
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The paper describes the improvements made to the NRC Watt-VA Transfer Standard and AC Source which are used to support the NRC Travelling Standard Program. With these improvements, NRC clients can now calibrate on site the voltage, current, active, reactive and apparent power functions of their standards for voltages of up to 600 V and currents of up to 50 A.

articleTitle: Technical objects external magnetic fields automatic measuring system
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The automatic measuring system of technical objects magnetic fields control measurements is developed. The high level of anticountermeasures from external object magnetic fields is achieved. The multifield measuring EMF noise influence on accuracy is eliminated. The methodic measuring error is reduced. The system has a flexible software, mobility and possibility of function modules interchange ability, it allows to make direct indirect and aggregate measurements.

articleTitle: Short time Fourier transforms and other transforms applied to the calibration of power analysers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the measurement of nonsinusoidal waveforms, in particular the use of waveform transforms in the calibration of power analyser instruments designed to make harmonic measurements to the requirements of the IEC standards on harmonics. The consequences of harmonics to electricity supply companies and users are considered. The paper then reviews the IEC standards regarding steady-state harmonics and fluctuating harmonics.

articleTitle: International comparison of power measurements at 33 GHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A BIPM international comparison of power measurements (GT-RF/92-4) has been carried out between eight national metrology laboratories at 33 GHz. The BNM-LCIE acted as pilot laboratory. The results show very good agreement in measuring effective efficiency and magnitude of reflection coefficient for the two IEC R320 waveguide thermistor mounts involved in the comparison.

articleTitle: Model tests to investigate the effects of geometrical imperfections on the NIST calculable capacitor
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A calculable capacitor links the U.S. capacitance unit to the SI unit and has a relative standard uncertainty of 2/spl times/10/sup -8/. Geometrical imperfections are one of the largest sources of this uncertainty. Tests with a model calculable capacitor have been done to better evaluate and reduce this uncertainty.

articleTitle: The effect of residual adsorbed gases on silicon isotope amount ratio measurements [in Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. An adsorption model developed for molecular flow inlet system was applied successfully to remove memory effects in high accuracy isotopic measurements, especially in the Si isotopic measurements leading to improved values for the Avogadro constant.

articleTitle: Frequency standard based on /sup 192/OsO/sub 4/ /spl nu//sub 3/P(46)A/sup 2//sub 2/ fundamental line
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. We report the frequency value of the /sup 192/OsO/sub 4/ ν/sub 3/P(46)A/sup 2//sub 2/ line, measured with respect to the hot line absorption in coincidence with the same CO/sub 2/ 10P(14) line, using a transportable CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ standard.

articleTitle: Development of a precision one ohm resistance standard
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: This paper describes the design and fabrication of a one ohm standard resistor. It utilizes the same techniques and materials that are used in the 100 ohm SR102, the 10 kohm SR104 and the 6,453.20 ohm standards that have been used in the quantum Hall effect work.

articleTitle: Frequency comparison of /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A first international comparison of I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers has been made between National Research Laboratory of Metrology (NRLM, Japan) and Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics (JILA, USA). The results of the comparison show that the Allan variance of the portable NRLM laser has reached <3/spl times/10/sup -13/ when the integration time is larger than 100 s. Frequency difference between the NRLM laser and the JILA laser is 3563 Hz (of IR light) with the matrix-averaged standard deviation of about 310 Hz.

articleTitle: Frequency noise measurements of lasers locked to a rubidium mastered optical cavity
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: A small, evacuated, piezoelectrically-tuned Fabry-Perot cavity is stabilized using a commercial rubidium oscillator. The cavity's resonance is measured and controlled using two diode-pumped Nd:YAG lasers; each locked to a mode of the cavity. Once controlled the cavity resonance acts as a frequency reference for the lasers. To measure the laser frequency noise, one of the laser beams is combined with a laser beam from an identical system. The beat frequency between the two lasers allows a measure of the linewidth, frequency noise and root Allan variance of a single laser. This data is reported and compared to results from more elaborate laser frequency control schemes.

articleTitle: A set of waveguide primary thermal noise standards and related calibration systems for the frequency range 8.2-40 GHz
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: The national metrology laboratory, BNM-LCIE, has developed, a set of four new waveguide primary thermal-noise standards for frequencies between 8.2 GHz and 40 GHz. The output noise power obtained by making temperature and attenuation measurements is within (948-1012) K/spl plusmn/(1.2-1.8) K (1 /spl sigma/). The standard-type uncertainty of 14-16 dB ENR sources calibrated with switching radiometers is less than 0.02 dB.

articleTitle: Quantum efficiency measurement of photodetectors by means of correlated photons
publicationTitle: 1998 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest (Cat. No.98CH36254)
abstract: We report the first results concerning quantum efficiency measurement of photodetectors with the technique of correlated photons generated by parametric down conversion in a nonlinear crystal. Measurements have been performed on photomultipliers in photon counting regime and will be extended to avalanche photodiodes working as single photon detectors.
